However, it is unclear whether the task qualifies as an executive function domain (I6 not confirmed — sequencing/motor preparation may not map cleanly to working memory/inhibition/cognitive flexibility/planning/vigilance/initiation), whether whole-brain voxelwise group-level maps are reported (I7 not confirmed), and whether a within-group task contrast is reported (I8 not confirmed). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly met based on the abstract. Because the full text is incomplete and key inclusion criteria cannot be verified, I exclude this study pending full-text review.

Although this paper uses fMRI with group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (black faces > baseline; black > white) and reports whole-brain coordinates, it does not implement an explicit executive-function task in the scanner. The fMRI paradigm was a spatial-location perceptual task (indicating left/right presentation of faces); the Stroop inhibitory task (an established executive function assay) was administered behaviorally in a separate session outside the scanner. Therefore the study does not meet the key inclusion requirements that (I5) the fMRI/PET study assesses executive function or cognitive control using a task-based paradigm in the scanner, and (I6) the in-scanner task fall within established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Met inclusion criteria: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI task-based study of cognitive flexibility (task switching), meeting the review objective. It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (62,980-voxel mask; voxelwise regressions and group t maps with cluster correction) and presents results in figures and tables (Table 1, Figs. 1–3). Within-group contrasts/analyses are reported (trial-evoked switch vs repeat paired t tests and voxelwise regressions of pretrial signal predicting RT performed within subjects and tested at group level). Participants and methods are described in full. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and is suitable for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study that includes a canonical executive function task (Go/No-go) probing response inhibition, reported as within-subject, within-group contrasts (No-go vs Go). Imaging used whole-brain, voxelwise, random-effects analysis (SPM2) with reported statistical maps, tables, and figures (coordinates and cluster results), satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. Other tasks are secondary but do not preclude inclusion. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing verification of analyses. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (WM > control; spatial vs object contrasts) with whole-brain voxelwise statistics and cluster-correction, and reports regional results in figures and supplementary tables. Within-group task contrasts (WM vs control and task-type contrasts) are explicitly reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (imaging and fMRI analysis), Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete: only title/abstract/metadata provided. The abstract confirms this is an fMRI study of Stroop conflict (so I5 and I6 are met). However the provided content does not allow verification of required whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level task activation results (I7) nor explicit reporting of at least one within-group task contrast (I8); I10 (acceptable formats) also cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria are clearly met from the abstract. Because core methods/results needed to confirm all inclusion criteria are missing, the study cannot be included on the available evidence. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6. Inclusion criteria not met/ not verifiable: I7, I8, I10. Exclusion criteria met: none. Please provide complete full text or the group-level voxelwise contrast details to reconsider inclusion.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (working memory, n-back) in patients and controls. It reports within-group 2-back > 0-back voxelwise contrasts for both groups and group-level random-effects analyses with whole-brain coverage and coordinates/tables of activation maxima. Results are presented as voxelwise statistical maps (SPM/SnPM) and reported in tables/figures. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of planning using the Tower of London (an executive function task). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses (main effect of task, easy vs difficult, and within-group effects for males and females) with thresholding and tables/figures, and includes within-group contrasts (task > control/rest). Participants are healthy adults and the full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. The study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not a non-empirical paper. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive function (set-shifting/planning). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical analyses (mixed-effects/random-effects, voxelwise thresholds and Talairach normalization) and provides coordinate/figure-based reporting of activation peaks. Multiple within-group task contrasts are presented (e.g., retrieval with shift vs control; retrieval with shift vs retrieval without shift; continuous shift vs retrieval without shift), satisfying the requirement for within-group task contrasts. Participants are a healthy adult sample, which is acceptable. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a stop-signal task (inhibition) — an established executive function domain. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, random-effects group contrasts (e.g., stop success > stop error; stop > go) with whole-brain analyses and coordinate tables/figures. Thus it meets I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (inhibition), I7 (group-level voxelwise/whole-brain results), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinates/figures). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; not truncated. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, and is empirical).

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract, the study is an empirical fMRI task study of working memory, satisfying inclusion criteria I5 and I6. However, the available content does not allow verification of required whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps (I7), nor confirmation of at least one within-group task contrast (I8), nor whether whole-brain results are reported in acceptable formats (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are demonstrably met from the abstract alone. Because core methods/results are not available to confirm I7 and I8, the study cannot be confirmed as eligible. Therefore I exclude it pending full-text access.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a Stroop color-word task, which assesses cognitive control/inhibition (executive function). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level composite statistical maps (t-tests, correlation analyses) contrasting incongruent versus congruent trials (i.e., a within-group task contrast). Although slice coverage was limited (10 slices), partial-brain acquisition is allowed provided voxelwise analyses are reported — which they are. Results are presented as whole-brain composite maps and ROI tables/coordinates. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This article is a computational/simulation study modeling PFC mechanisms and reproducing fMRI-like signals from an integrate-and-fire network; it does not report original task-based human fMRI or PET group-level, voxelwise activation maps or within-group task contrasts. Exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical papers/simulations without original human neuroimaging data) applies. Inclusion criterion I6 (working memory task domain) is met because the paper models working memory delay tasks. However I5 (original fMRI/PET task-based study), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level analysis), and I8 (within-group task contrast) are not met. Full text appears to be abstract-level content rather than complete methods/results, so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an empirical fMRI study that reports within-group, voxelwise task activation contrasts probing executive resources (working memory and planning/decision-making) during sentence disambiguation. The authors performed random-effects, whole-brain SPM2 analyses and present voxelwise contrasts (e.g., less-consistent vs more-consistent; with WM vs without WM) with coordinates and figures. The task manipulations fall squarely within executive function domains (working memory and planning), and group-level voxelwise results are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and appendices, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (a core executive function) using a stop-signal paradigm. It reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses (successful vs failed stop trials; one-sample t test across 24 subjects and group-wise median-split contrasts), with tables/figures of coordinates and statistical maps. Participants are healthy adults. The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study reports only ROI-based analyses and does not provide a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (only ROI analyses). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function/cognitive control), I6 (working memory/inhibition task within executive domains), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant group acceptable). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task-evoked statistical map reported). Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, but the analytic approach is confined to anatomically defined ROIs and voxelwise/whole-brain maps are not presented; therefore the study does not satisfy the whole-brain voxelwise result requirement and must be excluded.

Full text is incomplete (only title and abstract provided). From the abstract, this is an fMRI study of working memory and attention tasks (I5, I6) and reports item-related responses assessed relative to an attention condition, indicating within-group task contrasts (I8). However, the available content does not allow confirmation that group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps are reported (I7) or that voxelwise results (coordinates/figures/tables) are provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met. Because I7 cannot be verified from the provided incomplete full text, the study cannot be confirmed to meet all inclusion criteria and is therefore excluded pending full-text availability.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (stop-signal paradigm) directly probing an executive function domain (inhibition). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., StopInhibit > Go) with thresholded maps, coordinates, conjunction analyses, and ROI summaries. Within-group contrasts are explicitly reported for the healthy subject group across Manual, Letter Naming, and Pseudoword Naming tasks. Results are presented as voxelwise maps and coordinates (tables/figures), satisfying the reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive function (response inhibition) using a Go/No-Go task (I5, I6). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise group-level activation maps (No-Go vs Oddball and related contrasts) computed with whole-brain, cluster-level nonparametric analysis and provides coordinate tables and figures (I7, I8, I10). The participant group (healthy adults) is acceptable (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROI-only analyses, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and not solely between-group contrasts. Full article content (background, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for pooling of task-evoked executive function activations.

This study is an event-related fMRI investigation using a Stroop task (an established inhibition/cognitive-control paradigm) and reports voxelwise, group-level task-evoked statistical maps and time-course p-maps. It provides within-group task contrasts (incongruent stimuli-related activations) for both pathological gamblers and healthy comparison subjects, with voxelwise analyses and reported activations in figures/tables. Although slice coverage was limited (10 oblique axial slices), the methods describe voxelwise whole-brain stereotactic mapping and explicit checks for susceptibility artifacts; partial-brain acquisition is acceptable per criteria. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of interference control (numerical Stroop), directly addressing inhibition (an executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM2 analyses including within-group contrasts (distance and congruity effects), baseline contrasts, conjunction analysis, and tables/coordinates of whole-brain activations. Participant groups include a clinical sample (MCI) and controls. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, discussion and activation tables, indicating completeness. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts) apply. Thus the study satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for inclusion.

This Nature Protocols article describes the counting Stroop task and its use in fMRI/PET studies but does not present original group-level voxelwise neuroimaging results. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical/methods paper without original human neuroimaging data). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (task falls within established executive function domains — cognitive interference/inhibition). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the paper is not an original fMRI/PET empirical study reporting new activation results), I7 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical maps or reported coordinates in this article), I8 (no within-group task contrast results are reported here), I9 (no within-group neuroimaging contrast reported for any participant group in this paper), I10 (no qualifying whole-brain results presented in text, tables, or figures). Full text appears complete (protocol with introduction, methods, anticipated results) so fulltext_incomplete=false. Given these gaps, the article should be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on pooling task-evoked activation maps.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the Stroop task (inhibition/cognitive control), reporting voxelwise whole-brain GLM analyses and group-level activation maps. The paper provides within-group task contrasts (conflict-related activity for controls and for unaffected relatives), reports whole-brain results in tables/figures, and describes preprocessing and cluster-thresholding for voxelwise inference. The task falls within executive function/inhibition domain. It is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and includes within-group contrasts for multiple participant groups. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based paradigms (N-back, WCST, CPT) that probe executive functions (working memory, cognitive flexibility, vigilance). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (2-back > 0-back one-sample t-test and regression analyses using SPM2) with tables/figures of activation peaks and corrected results, satisfying a within-group task contrast. The sample is a participant group (healthy young adults) which is acceptable. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using the color–word Stroop (a well-established inhibitory/cognitive control executive function task). It reports within-group, event-related contrasts (e.g., incongruent > congruent; congruent+incongruent > neutral) analyzed with group random-effects voxelwise statistics (thresholding and cluster extent reported). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and results are described in text, figures, and tables. Although acquisition used limited slices (13 contiguous slices), the inclusion criteria explicitly allow partial-brain acquisitions provided analyses are voxelwise, which is satisfied here. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so core article content is present.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using an n-back working memory paradigm (an established executive function domain). The paper reports within-group voxelwise task contrasts (1-back>0-back, 2-back>0-back) using whole-brain SPM analyses with cluster-level correction and provides coordinates/tables and figures of activation maps. Multiple participant groups (including schizophrenia and APD) are included, and within-group activation maps are reported for each group. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is an empirical study). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion; key analyses and coordinates are reported. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study investigating cognitive control (thought/image suppression, erasing, imagining) that involves inhibition and visual working-memory/updating processes. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., suppressing > free-thinking; erasing > free-thinking; imagining > free-thinking). Healthy adult participants were studied. Results are reported as voxelwise activations (figures/tables) and correlations with behavioral measures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study that directly assesses cognitive control/conflict (Stroop and Simon interference tasks) using task-based paradigms. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise statistical maps (incongruent vs congruent contrasts), including whole-brain (albeit limited-slice) voxelwise analyses, time-course maps, and Talairach coordinates. It includes within-group contrasts (incongruent > congruent) for healthy adult participants and reports results in figures/tables. The full text contains introduction, detailed methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and no exclusion criteria are met.

The study reports an fMRI task (Color–Word Matching Stroop) targeting inhibitory control, an established executive function domain. The abstract describes a within-group, group-level contrast (incongruent vs neutral) and reports differential whole-brain activations (frontoparietal network), indicating voxelwise task-evoked results appropriate for inclusion. However, only the abstract/metadata are provided here (no full methods/results sections), so fulltext_incomplete is flagged and certainty is moderate. Inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 appear satisfied based on available information; no exclusion criteria are met in the available content.

This is an empirical PET/fMRI study that includes a task within the executive function domain (working memory: 2-back verbal task) and episodic memory tasks. Group-level, voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM voxelwise ANCOVA for PET; group activation maps for fMRI) and within-group task contrasts (e.g., 2-back vs control/0-back and encoding/retrieval vs baseline) are described. Participant groups (young and old volunteers) have within-group contrasts. Reporting is whole-brain voxelwise and described in methods/results. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the N-back working memory task (an established executive function). The manuscript reports whole-brain BOLD acquisition and voxelwise analyses using SPM99, individual subject one-sample t maps and group-level (random-effects) ANOVAs, and reports voxelwise results in figures/tables (coordinates). Within-group task contrasts (e.g., 2-back vs 0-back) are described and used to generate second-level analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and thus appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study of cognitive switching (cognitive flexibility), an executive function domain. It reports a within-group, voxelwise group analysis (group‐level GBAM produced via permutation testing and cluster-level inference) contrasting switch vs repeat trials (a within-group task contrast). Whole-brain acquisition and analyses are described, with results reported in text, tables, and figures. Participants are healthy adults but inclusion accepts any participant groups. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and conclusions, so full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly investigates initiation (an executive function domain) using an event-related paradigm. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM second-level random effects and thresholded maps), within-group task contrasts (e.g., planning internally-initiated vs rest; internally- vs externally-initiated planning), and provides coordinates and temporal SPM maps. Participants are a healthy adult sample (within-group contrasts reported). Reporting includes whole-brain results and ROI checks but is not limited to ROI-only analyses. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of an n-back working memory task (an executive function) with task-based activation contrasts. It reports voxelwise t-tests (condition vs fixation) used to generate activation maps, presents group-averaged t maps for the 2-back>rest contrast (figures), provides Talairach coordinates/centroids (Table 2), and reports within-group task contrasts and ROI-based group statistics. Participants include clinical (high-functioning autism) and matched controls; within-group contrasts are reported for at least one group. Thus the study meets criteria I5 (fMRI task-based), I6 (working memory), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain maps shown/coordinates reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant groups allowed), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive functions (SART) assessing inhibition, sustained attention, error processing (meets I5,I6). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise statistical maps (voxelwise t-tests with cluster thresholds, Talairach normalization) and presents whole-brain event-related and block activation maps in tables/figures (meets I7,I10). Within-group contrasts are reported (Random vs Fixed SART, correct inhibitions and error-related contrasts vs baseline; main effects of task against rest are reported) satisfying I8. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample (I9). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (nogo vs saccade), which falls within executive function (inhibition). It reports within-group voxelwise, mixed-effects group-level statistical maps (instruction and response contrasts) computed across subjects, with cluster correction. Although slice coverage was partial (axial slices to dorsal caudate/thalamus), analyses are whole-brain voxelwise within the imaged volume and therefore meet the partial-brain allowance. The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion and provides coordinate/cluster tables and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical).

This is a task-based fMRI study that reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps for executive function tasks. It assesses working memory (two-back) and cognitive flexibility/set-shifting (speeded WCST), which are established executive domains, and includes a within-group task vs control contrast. The analysis used voxelwise t-statistic maps normalized across subjects (21-slice EPI acquisition—partial-brain but voxelwise), with reported ROIs, tables, and figures describing whole-brain results. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical, event-related fMRI study using a Stroop color-word matching task (inhibition domain of executive function). The paper reports whole-brain acquisition and voxelwise group-level (random-effects) analyses contrasting incongruent vs. neutral conditions (within-group task contrast), with activation tables/figures and timecourse analyses. Participant groups and methodology are clearly described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study should be included in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Full text provided appears incomplete (only title and abstract/metadata). Based on the abstract, the study meets some inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (task involves inhibition — go/no-go animal detection), and I8 (within-group task contrast: targets vs distractors). However, I cannot verify key required criteria from the incomplete text: I7 (presence of a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map) and I10 (clear reporting of whole-brain results in coordinates/figures/text). The abstract reports activations in multiple brain regions but does not provide enough detail to confirm a voxelwise group analysis or that whole-brain results are reported in a usable form. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met from the abstract. Because the full text is incomplete, I must exclude this record pending full-text review; the exclusion is due to inability to confirm I7 and I10 from available content.

This fMRI study used a task-based N-Back working memory paradigm (an executive function domain) and reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses. The methods describe creation of SPM{T} maps and a random-effects, within-subject one-way ANOVA using task contrasts (e.g., 3-back minus 1-back) and report MNI coordinates for significant clusters. Although the authors limited the search volume to an a priori ROI and applied small-volume correction, voxelwise group-level task-evoked maps and within-group contrasts are clearly reported. Participants are a defined group of smokers. Core article content (introduction, full methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses contrasting task periods (retrieval/manipulation) against maintenance, corrected for multiple comparisons (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures), and also reports within-group contrasts (manipulation vs retrieval and task vs maintenance). Thus it provides qualifying within-group task activation maps from a task in the executive-domain. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

Full text provided is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata). The abstract indicates the paper reports PET and fMRI data and discusses vigilance/sustained attention (so I5 and I6 appear satisfied). However, I cannot verify crucial eligibility requirements: there is no available information to confirm whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps (I7), nor that any within-group task contrast is reported (I8). I also cannot confirm reporting format (I10) or participant/contrast details (I9). Because the full text is incomplete and key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed, the study is excluded from the meta-analysis at this stage. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are positively met based on the provided content.

This study reports task-related changes in mutual information (functional connectivity) during an N-back working memory task but does not present any group-level, voxelwise task-evoked activation maps. Instead analyses are ROI-based (90-region parcellation) connectivity comparisons between rest and task. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E4 (connectivity-only analyses without task activation maps) and E3 (analyses are region-based rather than voxelwise whole-brain activation). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task study), I6 (working memory task = executive function), I8 (within-group task contrast comparing rest vs N-back for connectivity), I9 (healthy participant group). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical activation map reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study assesses planning (Tower of London) in healthy adults and reports within-subject contrasts (Difficult vs Control; Easy vs Control) and group comparisons, so I5, I6, I8 and I9 are satisfied. However, the paper does not present a group-level voxelwise task activation map; analyses are based on individually-derived t-maps quantified within manually defined volumes-of-interest (VOIs) and between-group comparisons were performed on VOI summary measures (spatial extent percentages). Thus it reports ROI-based/group ROI statistics rather than a voxelwise whole-brain group-level activation map. Exclusion criterion E3 is therefore met. Inclusion criterion I7 (at least one group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map) is not met. Full text appears complete. Decision: EXCLUDED (reason: E3).

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation using n-back working memory tasks (letters, shapes, locations), which directly addresses executive function (working memory). The abstract describes voxelwise statistical comparisons of activation patterns across stimulus types, implying group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses and within-group task contrasts. Therefore it appears to meet inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the provided ‘full text’ is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata are present), so I cannot verify detailed methods/results or confirm tables/figures of whole-brain results; thus I flag fulltext_incomplete=true and assign moderate confidence.

This manuscript is a methodological/review-style paper that illustrates covariance-based analyses (structural equation modeling and PLS) using PET data examples, rather than reporting standard task-evoked, group-level voxelwise activation maps. It focuses on connectivity/covariance analyses and does not provide conventional within-group, voxelwise task activation contrasts or coordinate-based whole-brain activation tables required for inclusion. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria for connectivity-only/methods focus and being non-empirical/methods-review in nature.

The abstract reports an empirical task-based fMRI study using the Counting Stroop (an inhibition/cognitive-interference task) with within-subject interference vs. neutral contrasts and group-level fMRI results (significant ACC activation reported). This satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (executive function - inhibition/cognitive control), I8 (within-group task contrast), and I9 (within-group adult sample). The abstract also reports group-level statistical results (P ≤ 10^-4) consistent with a voxelwise group contrast and reports activation loci, meeting I7 and I10 likely; however, the full article text/figures/tables are not provided here. Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata available), so confidence is moderate. Full text should be obtained to verify voxelwise whole-brain maps and coordinate reporting before final data extraction.

This is an H2(15)O PET study using a task-based N-back working memory paradigm (executive function). It reports voxelwise, group-level SPM99 analyses (2-back minus 0-back) for within-group contrasts in both healthy controls and schizophrenic patients, with whole-brain activation maps, coordinates, and figures. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Thus all inclusion criteria for task modality, executive-domain task, whole-brain voxelwise analysis, within-group contrasts, participant groups, and reporting of whole-brain results are met. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an fMRI task study that includes an established executive-function task (incongruent color-word Stroop — inhibition/cognitive control) performed during scanning, and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation contrasts. The paper provides within-group task contrasts (e.g., distraction-specific map (PD+HD)>(P+H), pain-specific contrasts (P−H), (PD−HD), and (PD−HD)>(P−H)), uses voxelwise SPM99 analyses across subjects, and reports whole-brain results in the text and tables. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy volunteers. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using an emotional counting Stroop, a well-established inhibition/cognitive-control (executive function) paradigm. The paper reports group-level voxelwise nonparametric (KS) statistical maps and provides coordinates and corrected p-values for within-group contrasts (negative vs neutral; fixation vs task), satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting even though slice coverage was partial. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults and results are presented in text/figures/tables. All inclusion criteria for the review are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical fMRI task-based investigation using the Stroop task (inhibition/selective attention), which falls within executive function domains. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level statistical parametric maps (SPM99) and provides within-group task contrasts for both TBI patients and healthy controls (group activation maps, tables and figures). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (group pooled maps), and results are reported in tables/figures. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures).

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From available information: inclusion criteria met - I5 (PET task-based study), I6 (tasks involve working memory/time estimation within executive domains), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported: e.g., counting no auditory stimulation vs counting with auditory stimulation). However I7 (clear evidence of whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical maps) cannot be verified from the provided content, nor can I10 (reporting of whole-brain results in tables/coordinates/figures) be confirmed. No exclusion criteria E3-E6 are clearly met based on available info. Because the full text is incomplete and the key requirement I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results) cannot be confirmed, the study cannot be included at this stage.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (a core executive function). It reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Load 7 vs Load 3) analyzed at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise statistics (voxel-level threshold with cluster-level correction) and provides tables/figures of activated/deactivated clusters. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion (complete full text). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-groups-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based cognitive control paradigm (occluded target switching visual search) that probes executive functions (working memory, cognitive flexibility/switching, response preparation). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise group-level contrasts (e.g., target switching vs. non-switching) with FDR correction, tables and figures of voxel-wise results, and within-group task contrasts. Participant sample is healthy adults. Reporting includes voxel-wise maps/coordinates. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive function (planning) using the Tower of London task (I5,I6). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM5; second-level ‘planning vs. baseline’ and ‘task load’ contrasts) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster tables/figures (I7,I10). It includes within-group task contrasts (main effects of task and task-load across subjects) and within-pair comparisons (paired contrasts) satisfying the requirement for a within-group activation map (I8). Participant type (monozygotic twins, including some meeting OCD criteria) is acceptable per inclusion criteria (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and not only between-group contrasts. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates none.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of executive function (interference suppression and response inhibition) using a task-based paradigm (combined flanker and go/no-go). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise task contrasts (incongruent > neutral; no-go > neutral) analyzed with SPM99 and random-effects group analyses. Results include whole-brain voxelwise contrasts and regression analyses, with coordinates and cluster reports, and separate within-group maps for children and adults. Partial-brain acquisition is acceptable under I7 because voxelwise analyses were performed. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI executive-function activation maps and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and detailed experimental procedures).

The study is a PET task-based investigation of the WCST in healthy subjects and thus appears to meet I5 (PET, task-based), I6 (executive function: WCST - cognitive flexibility/working memory), I8 (within-group task contrasts vs control/baseline), and I9 (participant group qualifies). However, only title/abstract and metadata are provided here (full text incomplete), so I cannot verify that at least one group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis or coordinate reporting is present (I7 not confirmed) nor confirm details required by I10. Because I7 cannot be confirmed from the supplied content, the study cannot be confirmed to meet all inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met based on available information.

This is an event-related fMRI Stroop study of cognitive control with healthy adults that reports within-group task contrasts and coordinate results, but all voxelwise statistical testing was conducted within an a priori ROI mask (BA 24/32, 8/9/46, 7/40) rather than as whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps. Therefore it does not provide qualifying whole-brain voxelwise activation results. Exclusion ID E3 applies (reports only ROI/masked analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task of executive control), I6 (inhibition/cognitive control domain), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (eligible participant group), I10 (results reported with coordinates/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level task-evoked map; analyses confined to ROIs). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control using a stop-signal paradigm (executive function: inhibition). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task details, subjects, image acquisition, analysis), Results (group-level voxelwise activation maps, Bonferroni-corrected voxelwise threshold, coordinates table), and Discussion. The paper reports within-group task contrasts (GO ONLY vs GO/STOP; parametric STOP-likelihood analysis; correct vs incorrect STOP trials) at the group level using voxelwise statistical maps and provides coordinates and figures. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports behavioral task-switching data collected in three testing environments (including participants tested inside an operating MRI scanner) but explicitly states that brain-imaging data are not reported in this paper. Thus it does not provide any within-group, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or any reported fMRI/PET activation contrasts that could be pooled in the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (task falls within executive function domain: cognitive flexibility/task switching) and I9 (participant groups are acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no reported fMRI/PET activation results reported in the paper), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps provided), and I8 (no within-group task activation contrast reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) directly apply. Full text appears complete and includes methods, results, and discussion, but lacks imaging results needed for this meta-analysis, so the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (N-back), an executive function domain. It reports within-group voxelwise analyses (2-back > 0-back) with group-level whole-brain random-effects results (FWE-corrected maps) and ROI/SVC follow-ups. Methods, results, and discussion are present (full text complete). Therefore it meets all applicable inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the Stroop task, which assesses inhibition/action-monitoring (executive function), satisfying I5 and I6. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses using SPM (fixed- and random-effects), and provides within-group task-versus-control contrasts (one-sample t-tests) for both patients and controls, meeting I7 and I8. Participant groups include clinical OCD patients and healthy controls, acceptable per I9. Whole-brain results are presented in figures and tables of coordinates, satisfying I10. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present; fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical, event-related fMRI study using a Sternberg verbal working memory task (an established executive-function domain). The authors performed voxelwise, group-level random-effects analyses (one-sample t-tests) contrasting task vs control within participants for encoding, maintenance, and retrieval periods, and reported whole-brain activation foci (tables/figures), despite restricting reporting to ROIs and having incomplete inferior cerebellar coverage. These analyses satisfy within-group task contrasts and voxelwise group maps required by the review. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study using a graded n-back working memory paradigm (an established executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise GLM deactivation maps (random-effects t/maps thresholded at p=0.001) and group-level ICA components derived from whole-brain EPI data, and describes within-group task contrasts (task vs baseline and load-related effects across 0-, 1-, and 2-back). Participants are healthy volunteers (acceptable). Thus all required inclusion criteria are met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (working memory task), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of planning (an executive function) using the Tower of London paradigm. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (GLM, random-effects, FWE-corrected p<0.05, cluster extent threshold), contrasts of ToL versus two active control conditions (within-group task contrasts), and parametric within-group analyses across planning complexity; results are reported as coordinates/tables and figures. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a Stroop paradigm (cognitive control/inhibition) in healthy participants. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (e.g., IC vs CC contrasts), including tables/coordinates and ROI follow-ups, and presents within-group task contrasts (incongruent vs congruent and emotional word contrasts). These meet the meta-analysis requirements for executive-function task activations and do not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment of methods and contrasts.

The study reports task-based fMRI of verbal working memory (n-back) in healthy adults, with group-level voxelwise analyses and a within-group task contrast (n-back vs sensorimotor control). The paper describes whole-brain multislice acquisition, voxelwise sinusoidal regression and regression analyses relating fMRI response power to reaction time, and reports peak coordinates for activations. These satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group contrasts). Note: the provided full text appears incomplete (title and abstract/metadata only), so I flagged fulltext_incomplete=true and applied the inclusion criteria based on the available abstract and metadata.

This is a task-based fMRI study using the CPT-IP (a sustained attention/vigilance task), reporting within-group contrasts (CPT-IP vs control) and group composite voxelwise t-maps with voxel-by-voxel comparisons and cluster-based multiple-comparison correction. Whole-brain acquisition (24 contiguous slices covering most of the brain) and voxelwise analyses are described, and results are reported in figures/tables/text for both bipolar and healthy groups. Thus it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (vigilance/executive domain), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that examines working memory (n-back) and visual attention tasks with parametric load manipulations in 22 healthy adults. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2) with corrected thresholds and conjunction/subtraction contrasts, including within-group task contrasts (e.g., 2-back vs 0-back; 4-balls vs 2-balls) and ROI follow-ups. Working memory is an established executive function domain, satisfying the review focus. The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion, and whole-brain results are described and thresholded appropriately. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of executive function (working memory) using the Reading Span Test. It reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM99) with voxelwise thresholds and presents within-group task contrasts (Read+Memory and Recognition phases) and reported activation clusters/coordinates for young and elderly groups. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a digit n-back paradigm (working memory), an established executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise activation maps (group correlation analysis after stereotaxic transformation, thresholded and displayed), and within-group contrasts (0-, 1-, 2-back versus baseline/control) for multiple participant groups (euthyroid, hyperthyroid, SCH, hypothyroid). Whole-brain activation maps and figures are presented and described in the text. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-based, within-group, whole-brain voxelwise activation reporting are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that probes emotional conflict resolution — a form of cognitive control/inhibition — using a modified Stroop paradigm. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM random-effects contrasts (e.g., incongruent vs congruent; high vs low conflict-resolution), whole-brain/search-volume analyses, and within-group task contrasts in healthy volunteers. It therefore meets all inclusion criteria for an executive-function activation meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) that reports voxelwise whole-brain group analyses and within-group contrasts. The paper presents voxelwise ANOVAs, planned within-group contrasts (e.g., combination > object/location in young adults), Talairach coordinates, figures, and tables of activations. Although only 21 axial slices were acquired, the analyses are voxelwise (partial-brain acquisition is allowed). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI using a go/no-go variant probing inhibition and timing (executive function/cognitive control). It includes within-group one-sample voxelwise SPM analyses (controls) comparing unpredictable vs. predictable events and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with coordinates and statistics. Thus it provides voxelwise task-evoked maps and within-group contrasts for at least one participant group (controls), satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. Participant groups (ADHD, unaffected siblings, controls) are reported and any group is acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not limited to between-group contrasts. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (N-back), an executive function. The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses (group t-maps for 1-, 2-, 3-back vs 0-back) and provides within-group task contrasts for patient and control groups, with whole-brain voxelwise thresholding and reported peak coordinates. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

Full text incomplete. From the abstract, this is a PET task study of rapid visual information processing (sustained attention and working memory) and reports task vs rest activations in healthy volunteers, so it appears to meet I5 (PET task-based), I6 (vigilance/working memory), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (within-group healthy volunteers), and I10 (whole-brain results described in text). However, the provided full text is incomplete/missing, and I cannot verify that a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical analysis/map was performed or reported (I7). Because I7 cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, I exclude the study pending full-text verification.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: (I5) it is an fMRI task-based study of executive function (working memory 2-back); (I6) the task falls within an executive function domain (working memory); (I7) voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed (SPM-99, group-level maps reported; acquisition covered the brain with contiguous axial slices—partial or whole-brain acquisition allowed); (I8) within-group task contrasts are reported (WM vs vigilance within controls and within high-risk relatives; Figure 2 and text present these within-group activations); (I9) participant group is acceptable (adolescents/young adults; clinical high-risk relatives are permitted); (I10) whole-brain results are reported with coordinates and detailed tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, and within-group contrasts are provided). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore include the study for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract it is clear this is an event-related fMRI GO/NOGO task addressing inhibition and cognitive control, so inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are satisfied. However the supplied content does not allow confirmation of required whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps (I7) or explicit within-group task contrasts (I8). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) are evident from the abstract, but because not all inclusion criteria can be verified from the incomplete full text, the study cannot be included at this stage. Recommend obtaining the complete article to confirm I7 and I8 (and I10, if relevant).

This is an empirical fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (executive function domain) with healthy participants. The paper reports both within-group contrasts (parametric linear trend of load n within subjects and ROI time-series analyses) and a group-level, voxelwise random-effects map-wise analysis (normalized t-maps with whole-brain correction), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. The task and analyses clearly fall within the executive function domain (working memory), and results are reported in standard formats (text, figures, tables). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI task-based study using an auditory verbal N-back (working memory) paradigm (executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level random-effects SPM analyses (two-back vs zero-back), with within-group contrasts presented for each genotype and whole-brain results summarized in tables/figures including MNI coordinates and cluster statistics. Methods describe whole-brain preprocessing/normalization and voxel-by-voxel GLM analyses. Therefore it meets I5 (fMRI task-based executive function), I6 (working memory), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results presented in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive control (modified flanker) reporting group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and within-group task contrasts. The paper describes BOLD fMRI methods, SPM99 voxelwise contrasts (INC>CON, NOGO>CON and INC>NEU/NOGO>NEU), random-effects group analyses, and reports activation maps/tables and correlations. Participants (n=57 healthy adults) are acceptable. Results are presented in text, figures and tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion.

This is an fMRI, task-based study of context processing (AX-CPT) relevant to executive function (working memory/inhibition), with voxelwise group-level analyses reported (cluster-thresholded coordinates). However, the paper reports primarily between-group ANOVAs and group differences (B-cue, delay, and interaction) and does not present or describe a within-group task activation contrast (e.g., main effect of B cue vs implicit baseline) for any single group. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I9, and I10 but violates exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts reported with no within-group task activation contrast). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a modified Stroop task (an inhibition/selective-attention executive function paradigm). The paper reports within-group voxelwise activation maps (SPM99) for both patients and controls (Stroop activation vs rest), includes group-level random-effects comparisons, and provides whole-brain results in tables and figures. Although slice coverage was limited (15 slices), analyses were voxelwise and reported comprehensively. All required inclusion criteria for task, modality, within-group contrasts, and whole-brain voxelwise reporting are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) using a task-based Sternberg paradigm. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99 one-sample t-tests and random-effects ANOVA) with FDR-corrected thresholds and tables/figures of activated clusters/coordinates. At least one within-group task contrast is presented (memory task vs sensorimotor control and parametric contrasts of load and delay). Participants are human (healthy adults). Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, tables, and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing extraction of voxelwise task activation data for meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (working memory, response selection/conflict). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and within-group task contrasts (e.g., Repeat-Unexpected vs Repeat-Expected; Refresh vs Repeat), with coordinates and ROI analyses. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of semantic (category) verbal fluency that explicitly examines executive components (response inhibition, working memory, sustained attention) associated with paced vs. unpaced and overt vs. covert generation. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests, cluster-corrected p<.05) and within-group task contrasts (word generation overall and condition contrasts versus control/saying “nothing”). Participant group is healthy adults (acceptable). Results are reported in text, tables, and figures; full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of cognitive set-shifting (WCST variant) that reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical analyses and coordinates. It satisfies: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (cognitive flexibility/set shifting — an executive domain), I7 (group-level voxelwise analyses reported; partial slice coverage was used but voxelwise analysis was performed), I8 (within-group task contrast: shift-related activity vs pre-shift baseline), I9 (healthy adult participant group reported), and I10 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates and figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and references; fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI task-based study (MSIT) probing cognitive control/interference in healthy adults. The paper reports within-group voxelwise interference vs control contrasts at both individual and group levels, including group-averaged voxelwise t-tests in Talairach space and tables/figures of whole-brain activations. The task falls squarely within executive function/inhibition and cognitive control domains, and results include behavioral (RT, errors) and imaging maps. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is incomplete/unavailable (JSON error: API rate limit exceeded). Although the title mentions neural and cognitive measures of executive function, the methods and results are not accessible, so I cannot verify any required inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria not verifiable: I5 (no confirmation of fMRI or PET task-based imaging), I6 (task domain not clearly described as working memory/inhibition/etc.), I7 (no evidence of a group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis), I8 (no confirmation of a within-group task contrast), I9 (participant groups cannot be evaluated but this alone would not exclude the study), I10 (no reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables).
