This fMRI study uses a task-based 2-back working-memory paradigm with facial stimuli (an executive function: working memory) in patients and matched controls. The methods report voxelwise whole-brain group-level random-effects analyses (SPM99) and present within-group task activation results and tables/coordinates for each group, satisfying requirements for whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level maps and within-group contrasts. Participants include clinical samples (schizophrenia) which are acceptable. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not limited to between-group contrasts. Therefore inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that includes the Tower of London (planning) task, which is an established executive function domain. The paper reports group-level (random-effects) voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM) with results thresholded across the whole brain and presents activation maps and coordinate results for within-group contrasts (TOL easy and difficult vs yoked baselines). Healthy participant within-group contrasts are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the counting Stroop (inhibition/cognitive control) that reports voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses (AFNI, Talairach normalization, cluster-thresholding) and a within-group contrast (incongruent vs. congruent). Healthy adult participants were tested and results are reported in text/tables/figures (including coordinates and cluster results). The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations and should be INCLUDED.

This paper reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (two-back), an established executive function domain. Methods describe whole-brain EPI acquisition and voxelwise, group-level random-effects SPM99 analyses; results include within-group task contrasts for patients and controls, between-group contrasts, coordinate tables and figures. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Limitations. Thus all required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the n-back working memory task (an executive function domain). It reports within-group voxelwise whole-brain analyses (n-back conditions vs 0-back), trend analyses across loads, and presents group and within-group activation maps and coordinates. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an n-back working memory paradigm (executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2 random-effects one-sample t-tests) with coordinates/tables and figures for within-group task contrasts (e.g., L2–L1, NI–LI, NC–LC). Tasks fall within working memory domain; participant group (healthy adults) is included. Results include whole-brain statistical maps and ROI analyses but are not limited to ROI-only reporting. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical PET activation study using the Tower of London planning task (an established executive function: planning). The full text contains Introduction, Methods (PET acquisition, SPM voxelwise preprocessing and statistical analyses), Results (group-level category contrast: planning vs rest; correlation analyses of complexity and movement; tables/figures of whole-brain SPM results), and Discussion. The study reports within-group voxelwise task contrasts (planning minus rest and parametric correlations) suitable for inclusion. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses are performed and reported; partial brain coverage (field-of-view note) does not preclude inclusion per review criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and should be included.

Full text unavailable/incomplete: provided full-text content returns an API error and core article content (methods, results) is missing. Therefore I cannot verify required inclusion criteria. Unable to confirm: I5 (task-based fMRI/PET assessing executive function), I6 (task falls within established executive domains), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level maps), I8 (within-group task contrast reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable but within-group contrast unverified), I10 (results reported in coordinate/figure/text). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) can be determined from the incomplete record. Because core information is missing, the study cannot be confirmed to meet ALL inclusion criteria and is excluded pending full text. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/unknown: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the n-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). The full text reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level statistical maps (mixed-effects FLAME analyses) and provides within-group contrasts (e.g., 2-back>1-back, 2-back>0-back, 1-back>0-back) for both MDD patients and healthy controls. Results include cluster thresholds, Z-statistics and coordinate tables/figures. Although acquisition used 24 axial slices, analyses were voxelwise rather than ROI-limited. The study therefore meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a PET task study of motor planning (planning is an executive domain), with voxelwise parametric maps reported for a subject, but it does not provide a group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map. The report is a single-subject proof-of-principle (parametric maps and ROI results for one subject) rather than a group-level within-group contrast. Therefore it fails to meet I7 (group-level voxelwise map) and I8 (within-group task contrast at the group level). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based PET), I6 (planning task within executive domains), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (voxelwise/parametric results presented in text/figures). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (fixed-effect in Experiment 1; random-effect in Experiment 2) using SPM, with thresholding and cluster inference and peak coordinates provided. Within-group task contrasts (working memory task versus control) are reported and used in the group analyses. Results are presented as voxelwise subtraction images and coordinate tables/figures. The study is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and includes complete methods, results and discussion. Therefore it fulfills all inclusion criteria for task activation meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study that manipulates working memory load (two-back) and perceptual load using a task-based paradigm, and reports voxelwise whole-brain group analyses (with coordinates) comparing task conditions (e.g., two-back vs one-back). The study thus provides within-group task contrasts, includes working memory as an executive function domain, reports whole-brain voxelwise results (coordinates and thresholding), and includes participant group results. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of a working memory (executive function) task comparing structured vs unstructured sequences. The paper reports within-group, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FDR-corrected, peaks and coordinates reported) and supplementary ROI analyses; behavioral and control experiments are included. All required inclusion criteria are met (fMRI task-based executive function; working memory domain; whole-brain voxelwise group analyses with reported coordinates; within-group contrasts; participant group reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and experimental procedures).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that includes an executive function paradigm (color-naming Stroop, an inhibition/selective-attention task) and reports voxelwise, group-level statistical maps. The paper reports a within-group random-effects one-sample t-test for the motor task in controls, and reports group-level voxelwise two-sample (bipolar vs control) random-effects analyses for both motor and Stroop contrasts. Analyses were whole-brain SPM2 voxelwise maps with cluster correction and results presented in tables/figures. Participants include clinical (bipolar) and control groups; individual subject contrasts (task vs control conditions) were computed. Therefore the study meets I5 (task-based fMRI including an executive task), I6 (Stroop falls in inhibition/executive domain), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain maps), I8 (at least one within-group task contrast reported), I9 (clinical sample allowed), and I10 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level activation maps for mental arithmetic. The task includes a working-memory component (retaining intermediate results) and thus falls within an executive-function domain (working memory). The paper reports within-group contrasts (active math vs control) for musicians, non-musicians, and all subjects combined, with voxelwise random-effects analyses and figures/tables of coordinates. Results are whole-brain (composite activation maps and coordinate tables) rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI task study using a counting Stroop (inhibition/response conflict) paradigm with button-press responses. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise group-level activation contrasts (Stroop vs control) with whole-brain cluster correction and provides tables/figures of significant clusters. Although slice coverage is limited (19 sagittal slices), analyses were voxelwise and thus satisfy the partial-brain allowance. A within-group task contrast is clearly reported for healthy adult participants. Functional connectivity analyses are also present but do not preclude inclusion since task activation maps are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets I5–I10 and qualifies for inclusion.

Exclusion E3 met: the manuscript performs and reports ROI-based extractions/analyses of basal ganglia activation and volumetry, with statistical tests on ROI-derived measures (PAUC and volumes). While individual voxelwise timecourses were computed, the paper does not present or report group-level, voxelwise whole-brain (or partial-brain) task-activation statistical maps or coordinate tables; results and inferential statistics are ROI-focused. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study of executive/response control), I6 (task falls within executive domains — inhibition/set-shifting), I8 (within-group task contrast: correct target trials vs baseline/event-related activation), I9 (within-group contrasts reported for participant groups). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no clear group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported). Therefore the study must be excluded per E3.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an n-back working memory paradigm (executive domain) with healthy participants. The full text reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (one-sample t-test random-effects for 2-back vs 0-back and between-group ANOVA), including tables and figures of activations and cluster statistics. A within-group task contrast (2-back vs 0-back) is explicitly reported. The paper is empirical and contains complete sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria.

Exclusion E3 applies: the study reports fMRI working-memory task data but all reported analyses were ROI-based (authors state explicitly: “All the analyses reported... were performed with ROIs”), and no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps are presented. Inclusion met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory is an executive function), I8 (within-group task contrasts and paired t-tests reported), I9 (healthy participant group). Inclusion not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical map reported). Therefore the study must be excluded under E3.

The abstract describes an empirical task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (a canonical executive function) using a 2-back and match-to-center paradigm. The paper reports whole-brain fMRI activation patterns and explicitly describes within-group activation contrasts and patterns for both alcoholics and control groups, indicating voxelwise task-evoked maps. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (clinical participant group acceptable), and I10 (results appear reported in text/figures). However, only the abstract/metadata were provided here (no full methods/results/discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=true and there is some uncertainty (request full text to confirm voxelwise statistical maps/coordinate tables). Recommend retrieval of the complete article for definitive extraction and coordinate verification.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based verbal n-back working memory paradigm (executive function domain). It reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects GLM, voxelwise ANOVA, conjunctions) and within-group task contrasts (e.g., 2B>1B, task vs 0-back baseline, BSD>BRW). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Results are reported as voxelwise maps and ROI/peak coordinates. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back), an established executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (one-sample t-tests, full-factorial and paired t-tests) with whole-brain thresholds and MNI localization, and explicitly reports within-group task contrasts (2>0 and 3>0 back) for patients and controls. Clinical sample (severe diffuse TBI) is acceptable. Results are reported as activation maps/clusters and described in the text. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (N-back) for emotional prosody and lexico-semantic emotion in healthy adults. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM5 parametric and random-effects second-level analyses) with coordinates and thresholds, and includes within-group task contrasts (linear parametric increases with load; paired t-tests and conjunctions). Whole-brain acquisition and voxelwise results (tables/figures) are provided. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy young adults. Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive function fMRI and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control (executive function) using a simple warned RT paradigm (inhibition domain). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (one-sample t-tests, random-effects models) with whole-brain coverage and tables of coordinates and thresholded voxelwise results. Contrasts include within-group comparisons (e.g., cued vs no-cued; short vs long SOA) suitable as task activation maps. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of thought suppression, which constitutes an executive-control/inhibition paradigm. The paper reports within-group voxelwise, group-level statistical contrasts (e.g., SUPPRESS vs FREE-THOUGHT; CLEAR vs FREE-THOUGHT) analyzed with SPM99 and thresholded t-maps, with whole-brain coverage. Participants are healthy adults and results are described at the group level (brain regions/BA reported). Thus the study satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10, and none of the exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of attentional control/conflict (Simon and spatial Stroop), which falls within executive functions (inhibition/conflict). It reports voxelwise, random-effects group analyses (whole-brain contrasts: Simon Incongruent > Simon Congruent; Stroop Incongruent > Stroop Congruent), conjunction/disjunction and direct contrast maps, and describes cluster thresholds and peak locations (tables/figures). Within-group task contrasts are clearly reported for the healthy participant group. Results are presented as whole-brain activation maps and tables/figures rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of non-perceptual attentional set-shifting (cognitive flexibility), meeting the review objective. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM96 analyses (conjunctions and contrasts such as A–R, A–T, A–W, A–L) with whole-brain statistical thresholding and coordinates described. It reports within-group task contrasts (task vs rest and condition subtractions), uses healthy adult participants, and presents whole-brain results in the text (with coordinates). It is empirical and not ROI-only or connectivity-only. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an original, task-based fMRI study examining contextual inhibition (an executive function: inhibition). The paper reports within-group voxelwise whole-brain analyses (ACT vs REST, INH vs REST, conjunctions) with corrected statistical maps and tables/figures, and provides group-level results. Participants are healthy adults and contrasts are within-group. Whole-brain results are reported in text, figures, and tables of coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for an executive-function activation meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of inhibition (Go/Nogo) in schizophrenia that directly addresses executive function/cognitive control. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (complete). The study reports voxelwise, group-level statistical maps and corrected cluster thresholds (AFNI 3dDeconvolve and voxel-wise t tests), with tables of coordinates and figures for contrasts. It includes within-group task contrasts (e.g., Nogo–Go, Go/Cue–Go/Noncue, Cued-Nogo–Uncued-Nogo) and reports task-effect activations (task main effects) and correlations, satisfying within-group contrast requirement. Participants include a clinical sample (schizophrenia) and healthy controls; at least one within-group contrast is reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for pooling executive-function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the N-back working memory task (an executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses using SPM99 (thresholds and cluster criteria described), and contrasts of task vs control (0-back vs 2-back) were estimated at each voxel producing within-subject and group contrast images. Within-group task activations are described (e.g., severe cases showing bilateral parietal/OFC activations) and results are reported in tables/figures with coordinates. Participant groups include a clinical OCD sample and matched controls. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (executive function). The paper reports group- and within-subject voxelwise SPM99 analyses (random-effects ANOVAs), with whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (on-periods vs off-periods) and reported activation coordinates and clusters. Although slice coverage excluded the cerebellum, analyses were voxelwise rather than ROI-restricted. Results include within-group task activation maps for participants (MDMA users and controls) and coordinates are reported in the text and figures. Thus all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are satisfied, and none of the exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study (3T BOLD) that investigates Stroop-like inhibition paradigms (colour, number, shape), directly addressing the executive function domain of inhibition. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise first-level contrasts (congruent vs neutral; incongruent vs neutral) and a random-effects, second-level group analysis using SPM2, with whole-brain voxelwise results thresholded and coordinates reported in tables and text. Although ROI analyses are also performed, whole-brain voxelwise group maps and between-modality voxelwise comparisons are presented. Participant sample is a within-group (healthy adults). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a 2-back working memory paradigm (executive function domain), with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2, FDR-corrected) and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., Binding, Sign, Speech vs rest; Sign>Speech; 2Binding>Sign+Speech). Participants are a defined within-group (hearing native signers). Results are reported in tables and described in detail in the text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Appropriate for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a Stroop paradigm (inhibition/conflict-monitoring), clearly within executive-function domains. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses with whole-brain coverage and provides activation coordinates and corrected thresholds (FDR), and presents within-group task contrasts (conflict/incongruent vs congruent; conflict-level contrasts) and group-level task activation maps. EEG connectivity is additional but does not replace task activation reporting. Thus it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and within-group contrasts are reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study (1.5T) reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses of within-group task contrasts comparing normal vs malingered recognition responses. Although the primary task is recognition memory, the experimental manipulation and contrasts specifically target cognitive control processes (response suppression/inhibition, response generation, working memory/monitoring) during deceptive responding. Abstract and metadata indicate this is an fMRI task study using an auditory n-back (0-,1-,2-,3-back) probing working memory (an executive function domain). The paper reports brain activation patterns in response to increasing working memory load in MTBI patients and healthy controls and describes group-level activation differences and load-related modulation, which implies within-group task contrasts and voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked analyses typical for NeuroImage fMRI reports. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 appear satisfied. However, the provided content is limited to title/abstract/metadata (no methods/results figures/tables), so the full text is incomplete; I recommend obtaining the full PDF to confirm voxelwise statistical maps and coordinate reporting. No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

The article reports an empirical fMRI study using the counting Stroop (a well-established inhibition/cognitive-control executive task). It provides whole-brain, voxelwise GLM contrasts (e.g., number Stroop vs neutral during no-stimulation) and reports activation coordinates; within-group task contrasts are explicitly analyzed. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract metadata provided), so key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed. Based on the abstract, the study is an empirical task-based fMRI study (I5) that uses categorization tasks engaging executive processes (working memory, inhibition, attention) consistent with executive function domains (I6). The abstract reports within-group task contrasts (rule-based vs similarity-based; degraded vs similarity) satisfying I8, and participants are young adults (I9). However, I7 (presence of whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps) cannot be verified from the abstract alone, and I10 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in coordinates/figures/text) likewise cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met. Because the full text (methods/results) is missing, I cannot verify ALL inclusion criteria; therefore the study is excluded pending full-text review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the stop-signal task (an inhibition/cognitive-control paradigm). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses (FWE-corrected and uncorrected maps), contrasts of interest (post-go speeding > post-go slowing) at the group level, and presents results in figures/tables. Participants are healthy adults and the task falls squarely within executive-function (inhibition) domain. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and References. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function domain). The experiment reports within-group task contrasts (MAT, PREP, EXEC) with group-level statistics (ANOVAs and t-tests) and GLM-based voxelwise modeling. Although much analysis was ROI-focused, the authors also examined delay-period activity unconstrained by ROIs (whole-brain/unconstrained voxelwise search) and used a voxelwise FFA localizer, indicating voxelwise group-level analyses were performed. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy volunteers. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using an N-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) with within-group contrasts (working memory levels vs 0-back) and random-effects group-level statistical maps; results are described in text and figures (with SVC applied for multiple comparisons but based on voxelwise maps). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain executive-function activation reporting. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) in healthy adults, with task-based within-group contrasts and group random-effects (voxelwise) analyses and reported stereotactic coordinates and whole-brain maps. The full text contains introduction, methods (including whole-brain acquisition and GLM/group analyses), results, and discussion, so the article meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (modified PASAT) in TBI patients and controls, reporting voxelwise, group-level random effects analyses using SPM96 with whole-brain coverage. The manuscript presents within-group task contrasts (mPASAT vs control/baseline) for each group, reports activation maps and tables of coordinates (Table 2 and figures), and describes laterality and dispersion indices derived from voxelwise activation. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations (working memory) and provides whole-brain, within-group, voxelwise task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references).

This is an event-related fMRI empirical study of cognitive flexibility (task-switching) in OCD using a task-based paradigm. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (SPM2) including within-group contrasts (task-switch minus task-repeat) for each group, with coordinates and figures/tables of activations. The task falls squarely within the executive function domain (cognitive flexibility). Partial-brain acquisition (25 axial slices) is reported but voxelwise group analyses are provided, which meets I7. Results include within-group maps, between-group contrasts, ROI supplemental analyses, and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text is complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of auditory verbal working memory (an executive function). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses (within-group WM vs vigilance contrasts and whole-brain/random-effects analyses). Partial-brain acquisition (15 axial slices) is present but voxelwise analyses were performed, satisfying whole-brain/voxelwise requirement. Within-group contrasts are reported for groups. No exclusion criteria are met.

The full text reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (Stroop interference; inhibitory control) with healthy developmental participants. The paper includes within-group contrasts (incongruent vs congruent) and reports voxel-wise, group-level whole-brain (voxel-wise) analyses and maps/tables of age and performance correlations (voxel-wise regression with cluster thresholding). Although slice coverage was partial (only 6 slices used for all subjects), analyses were voxelwise rather than ROI-only. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Abstract reports an event-related fMRI study using three conflict tasks (including Stroop) with within-subject, within-group contrasts (incongruent vs congruent) and reports significant activations in anterior cingulate and prefrontal cortex, indicating task-based executive control (inhibition/conflict). This satisfies I5 (fMRI task-based), I6 (executive/inhibition tasks), I8 (within-group task contrast), and I9 (participant group acceptable). Full text is not provided (only abstract and metadata), so I cannot confirm whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses or the form of reported results (coordinates/figures) required by I7 and I10. Therefore I include the study provisionally for the meta-analysis, but with low confidence and fulltext_incomplete=true; recommend obtaining full article to confirm whole-brain voxelwise group maps and reporting details before final inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study that examines working memory (maintenance) and reasoning processes relevant to executive function. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99) with standard contrasts (reasoning vs rest, maintenance vs rest, reasoning vs maintenance) and provides coordinate-based results. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

Full text incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided); cannot verify required whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps. Based on abstract, study is an empirical fMRI working-memory task and reports within-group task contrasts: it satisfies I5 (fMRI study of executive function), I6 (working memory task), I8 (within-group task contrast), and I9 (participant group acceptable). However I7 (at least one group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis) cannot be confirmed from the provided content, and I10 (clear reporting of whole-brain results via coordinates/figures/text) also cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3,E4,E5,E6) are met based on available information. Because core article content (methods/results/discussion) is missing, I exclude pending full-text availability.

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (phonological rehearsal), which falls within the executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports single-subject and group-level voxelwise GLM analyses contrasting delay-period activity (L6 vs L1) and describes whole-brain group results (voxelwise), satisfying the requirement for a within-group task contrast and whole-brain task-evoked maps. Participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete for screening.

Although the study tested participants in an fMRI scanner, the article reports behavioral performance results (working memory and long-term memory) and does not present any task-evoked neuroimaging analyses, group-level voxelwise statistical maps, or within-group task activation contrasts. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria requiring a task-based fMRI/PET activation study with whole-brain voxelwise results (I5, I7) and a within-group task contrast (I8). The paper does meet that the tasks fall within an executive function domain (working memory; I6) and that it includes participant groups (young and elderly; I9). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The article reports an empirical fMRI study using a stop-signal task (inhibition — an executive function), with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and within-group contrasts (successful vs failed stop trials) reported in tables/figures and text. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text, and the study provides coordinates and group-level SPM results. Thus it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete.

This is a Nature Protocols methods paper describing the emotional counting Stroop task and how to implement it in fMRI; it does not present original empirical task-activation results or report group-level voxelwise statistical maps or within-group task contrasts. Therefore it is non-empirical/methods-only and does not provide the required whole-brain task activation analyses. Exclusion ID met: E6 (non-empirical/methods-only without original human neuroimaging data). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (task falls within executive function domains—Stroop-style inhibition/cognitive control). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no original fMRI/PET study reporting task activations), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). Full text appears complete for a protocol paper (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI task study of cognitive control (meets I5, I6) with within-group task contrasts reported and a healthy participant sample (meets I8 and I9). However, the imaging analyses reported are restricted to a priori ROI analyses (ACC and lPFC) rather than group-level, voxelwise whole-brain activation maps. The paper does not report voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses or coordinate tables for such maps, so it fails I7 and therefore meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using the color–word Stroop task (an inhibition/cognitive control/executive function paradigm) with within-group Stroop vs baseline contrasts. Group-level voxelwise statistical maps and Talairach-coordinate tables are reported; although slice coverage was limited, analyses were voxelwise and group-averaged label- and activation-maps are presented. Results include coordinates and figures of whole-brain (partial coverage) activation maps. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI study of executive function (visuospatial working memory n-back) (I5, I6), reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with corrected coordinates (I7, I10), and includes within-group task contrasts (2-Back minus Match-to-Centre; random-effects analyses) (I8). Participant group (young adults) is acceptable per I9. The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met: the paper includes whole-brain voxelwise activation results (not ROI-only), is not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and reports within-group contrasts rather than only between-group comparisons. Therefore INCLUDE.

This study reports task-based BOLD fMRI of a working memory task (an executive function domain). Methods describe voxelwise individual and group-level statistical parametric mapping (stimulus vs rest contrasts), whole-brain coverage (18 axial slices stated to encompass whole brain), group-average activation maps and thresholded voxelwise group analyses reported in tables and figures for each group. Therefore it provides within-group task contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results for clinical groups (AD, MCI, controls). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study of verbal working memory (n-back tasks), which is an established executive function domain. The paper reports within-group task contrasts (0-,1-,2-back; 1+2-back vs baseline; 2-back vs 1-back) using voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects analyses (SPM99), with cluster- and voxel-level inference and tables/figures of activation coordinates. Sample: 30 healthy adults. Therefore it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported in maps/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (2-back), an established executive function domain. It reports within-group, voxelwise GLM analyses at the group level (N=18), using whole-brain gradient-echo EPI (group one-sample t-tests and ANOVA), with activation maps described and shown. The contrast is task vs rest/implicit baseline (2-back vs rest), meeting the within-group task-evoked map requirement. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the Tower of London planning task (an executive function: planning). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99 random-effects models, cluster-level correction) and within-group task contrasts (e.g., six- vs four-move planning/execution; correct vs incorrect trials). Results include coordinates and tables/figures. Participants are a healthy student sample (within-group contrasts reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

The study is an event-related fMRI empirical investigation of planning (an executive function domain) using a task-based paradigm (Grid of Pittsburgh/Tower of Hanoi adaptation), satisfying I5 and I6. Analyses include group-level voxelwise tests of an ACT-R-derived task regressor (coefficient B2) and spatial t maps with coordinates and tables, meeting I7 and I10 (partial slice coverage reported but voxelwise group analysis performed). The reported group-level voxelwise contrasts correspond to within-group task effects (parametric modulation of planning load), satisfying I8. Participant sample is an adult within-group cohort (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and this is original empirical neuroimaging data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures). Therefore include.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that investigates response inhibition using somatosensory go/nogo tasks (executive function domain: inhibition). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM2) with whole-brain normalization, thresholding, and tables of activated coordinates for within-group contrasts (Movement Nogo vs baseline; Count Nogo vs baseline), satisfying requirements for task-evoked statistical maps. Results are presented in text, figures, and tables and the full article includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (visual object and spatial delayed-recognition tasks), meeting the executive-function domain. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise GLM analyses and spatially normalized group-average statistical maps (e.g., Delaylocation/no secondary task – baseline; Delayobject/no secondary task – baseline), and presents within-group task contrasts and group-level results (figures, tables, and coordinates). Participants are healthy adults and within-group contrasts are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (executive function domain) with voxelwise, group-level SPM2 analyses. The methods describe whole-brain preprocessing and random-effects group analyses; a conjunction of within-group contrasts ([3-back – 1-back] and [1-back – rest]) identified load-sensitive regions and results are reported in text, figures, and tables. Thus it provides within-group task contrasts, whole-brain voxelwise results (reported threshold and clusters), and qualifies across participant groups (young high/low and older adults). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (only ROI, only connectivity, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

Full text provided is incomplete (only title/metadata/redirect notice). From the title and metadata, the study appears to be an fMRI task examining semantic and phonological maintenance (likely working memory), so I5 (fMRI task) and I6 (working memory domain) appear satisfied. However, the methods and results are not available to confirm critical inclusion criteria: I7 (presence of group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (at least one within-group task contrast), and I10 (reporting of whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are identifiable from the available content. Because key inclusion criteria cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, the study is excluded pending access to the full article for verification.

This is an fMRI study with group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (semantic task vs control) and reports whole-brain results. However, the experimental paradigm is a lexico-semantic association/decision task, not an explicit executive function/cognitive control task. Although the authors discuss possible working memory demands, the task was not designed to probe established executive domains (working memory was neither manipulated nor the primary target). Therefore the study does not meet I5 (task assesses executive function/cognitive control) and I6 (task falls within established EF domains). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (whole-brain results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria are triggered (E3–E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete. Exclusion summary: excluded because I5 and I6 are not satisfied; other inclusion criteria (I7,I8,I9,I10) are satisfied.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a Stroop task (executive function: inhibition/cognitive control) with voxelwise, group-level random effects analyses reported (thresholded maps, cluster extent) and multiple within-group task contrasts (oddball vs baseline neutral; incongruent vs neutral; eligible vs ineligible). Partial slice coverage (10 slices) is present but the analyses are voxelwise at the group level, which qualifies under I7. Whole-text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Behavioral and imaging results are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

Exclusion E3 applies: the study reports ROI-based percentage signal change analyses and VOI/ROI statistics rather than a group-level voxelwise whole-brain task activation map or coordinate table. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function/working memory), I6 (working memory n-back task falls within executive function domain), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported, e.g., 1-back vs 3-back, single vs dual), I9 (within-group healthy adult sample reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no evidence of a group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical map; analysis was confined to anatomically-defined ROIs/VOIs), I10 (no voxelwise whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures/tables that would qualify). Full text appears complete. Because E3 is met, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis per the criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based antisaccade (inhibition) and ocular motor delayed response (working memory) paradigms that clearly probe executive function. The paper reports a voxelwise, group-level one-sample t test (whole-brain clustered map) comparing volitional saccade blocks vs fixation (task-evoked activation map), and reports within-group task effects (regions showing increased BOLD during volitional saccades) as well as group comparisons. Tasks fall within established executive domains (inhibition, working memory). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses and voxelwise thresholding/cluster correction are described. A within-group task contrast (task vs fixation) is reported (main effect of task), and clinical and healthy groups are included. The full text (background, methods, results, figures, discussion) is present. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study of task switching (executive function: cognitive flexibility) that reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects statistical maps (switch vs stay contrasts) with coordinates and thresholding; it also includes within-group task contrasts (switch>stay) for healthy participants. Partial slice coverage (20 slices) was used but voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed and reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) using an event-related paradigm with distractors. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses and a random-effects group-level contrast (memory-delay correct trials in distractor-plus vs control), with thresholding and activation coordinates reported. At least one within-group task contrast is presented; participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not a review). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and the study is eligible for inclusion.

This article reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of planning (Tower of London), an executive function, with both within-group (TOL vs fixation) and group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM99). The methods describe whole-brain preprocessing and group random-effects contrasts, and results include within-group activation maps, tables of coordinates, and figures. Partial slice coverage was used but voxelwise analyses were performed (acceptable per protocol). Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI executive function studies (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and within-group contrasts are reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cognitive control (cognitive reappraisal) using a task-based paradigm. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level SPM analyses (thresholded, coordinates in tables/figures) and within-group task contrasts (increase>look; decrease>look), with adult participants. Results include whole-brain activations and small-volume amygdala analyses but are not limited to ROIs. Therefore it satisfies I5 (fMRI cognitive control task), I6 (task involves cognitive control/executive processes such as interference resolution/inhibition/working-memory-like processes), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain group maps reported), I8 (within-group contrasts reported), I9 (participants reported), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of deception that engages cognitive control/inhibitory processes. The paper reports within-group voxelwise whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses (contrasts: lie>truth, lie>control, etc.) across 14 healthy adults, with coordinates and thresholding described and results reported in text/figures. Thus it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI of cognitive control), I6 (task involves inhibition/cognitive control), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI task study of picture–word (lexical) interference and language production, not an executive-function task. While the study includes whole-brain, voxelwise, within-group contrasts and reports results in tables/figures, the experimental task does not fall within established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I5 and I6. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group reported), I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does not assess executive function/cognitive-control as primary task), I6 (task is language/lexical processing, not an EF domain). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study directly addressing cognitive control/executive function (temporal integration, sustained maintenance, strategy representation). It uses whole-brain, voxelwise GLM analyses (state/item mixed design) with group-level random-effects tests and reports clusters/coordinates; within-group task contrasts are reported (task vs fixation; W2 vs W12; WIN×DYN interactions). Participants are healthy adults. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical simultaneous EEG–fMRI study using a task-based mental arithmetic paradigm that probes central executive processes (working memory, manipulation, sequencing). The paper reports voxelwise group-level fMRI analyses (SPM99 preprocessing, one-sample t-tests across n=8, whole-brain normalization and smoothing) and presents task contrasts (arithmetic vs rest) and phase-synchronization–related regressors producing statistical maps and tables of activated/deactivated regions. Thus it provides within-group task contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results relevant to executive function activations. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment against inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study of task-switching (cognitive flexibility), reporting within-group task contrasts (switch vs repeat) and group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (group t-tests on normalized beta-maps) that identify a left superior parietal region. The paper contains complete methods, results, and discussion enabling extraction of task-evoked activation loci. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a verbal working memory (n-back/2-back style) paradigm in schizophrenia and healthy controls. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. It reports voxelwise, whole-brain analyses (FPQ maps, generic brain activation maps, voxelwise ANOVA and permutation testing) and presents within-group task contrasts (activation vs baseline) for each group, with regional coordinates and figures/tables. Thus it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory = executive function), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analyses, partial coverage is acceptable), I8 (within-group task contrast reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical whole-brain fMRI study using a task-based oddball paradigm that probes attentional control and working-memory updating (executive domains: vigilance/working memory). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise one-sample t-test analyses (familywise error corrected) and within-group task contrasts (targets and novels vs implicit baseline) as well as parametric modulation by target/novel interval. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps and peak coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of phonological working memory (an executive function domain). It reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (WM vs control) using SPM2 random-effects whole-head analyses, with results described in tables and figures (stimulus-encoding, maintenance, comparison phases). Participants are healthy adults. The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Full text is incomplete (API error message provided), so core article content (methods/results) cannot be verified. From title/metadata, this appears to be an fMRI working-memory task study, satisfying inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI/PET assessing executive function) and I6 (task is working memory). However, I cannot confirm required criteria: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level statistical maps), I8 (a within-group task contrast reported), I9 (within-group contrast present for at least one participant group), or I10 (reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are demonstrably met from the available information (E3–E6 not confirmed). Because the full text is missing and critical inclusion criteria cannot be verified, the study is excluded pending access to the complete article.

The study reports a task-based fMRI investigation of working memory (an established executive function domain). It provides within-group, voxelwise group-level contrasts (memory vs control; manipulable vs non-manipulable) and reports whole-brain results with coordinates and figures. Although functional acquisition used limited axial slices, I7 allows partial-brain acquisition so long as voxelwise analyses are reported — which they are (random-effects, Talairach-transformed z-maps, cluster criteria). All required inclusions are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study that directly assesses working memory (an established executive-function domain) and episodic memory using task-based paradigms. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses and mapwise thresholds across the whole brain (with stereotactic coordinates and conjunction analyses), and presents within-group task contrasts (encoding, delay, recognition phases vs. ITI/baseline). Participant group (healthy adults) is included and qualifying. Results are reported as whole-brain maps and coordinate tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an event-related and blocked-design fMRI study that explicitly investigates executive functions (attention-switching and response inhibition) using task-based paradigms. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, random-effects whole-brain analyses (switch−nonswitch; incompatible−compatible; High-Switch−Low-Switch) with FDR correction and provides peak coordinates/tables and figures. Participants are a human within-group sample (undergraduates). Results are reported at the group level and voxelwise and thus meet the meta-analysis requirements. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is a task-based fMRI study of task-switching and endogenous control (executive function: cognitive flexibility/working memory). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects contrasts (e.g., transition cue vs task cue) with Z-maps, cluster thresholds, and tables of coordinates; within-group task contrasts and main effects are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study used a task-based, within-group word-retrieval (verbal fluency/word generation) paradigm that engages executive processes (initiation, search, sustained attention/working memory). The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects, voxelwise group analyses (task vs baseline and difficulty contrasts) with coordinates and figures, meeting requirements for group-level voxelwise maps. Participants are a defined within-group (healthy adults). Results and methods are fully reported (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria for executive-function-related activation (initiation/attention), whole-brain voxelwise analyses, and within-group contrasts.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that probes top-down attentional control and deliberate shifts of attentional set between feature dimensions. The paradigm directly assesses cognitive control/set-shifting (cognitive flexibility), an established executive-function domain. The study reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (e.g., shift vs hold) analyzed with a random-effects GLM across whole-brain volumes and provides Talairach coordinates and figures of activations. Participants are healthy adults and the paper includes full methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study is an empirical PET (15O-water) task-based activation study using the N-back verbal working memory task in healthy volunteers and reports activation maps across working-memory load. Based on the abstract, it meets inclusion criteria: I5 (PET task-based study), I6 (working memory in established executive domain), I8 (within-group task contrast / parametric N-back effects), I9 (participant group reported), and I10 (whole-brain results reported as activation maps). I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain evidence) appears to be met because the abstract refers to activation maps from ECAT HR+ across volunteers, but the full text is not provided here to unequivocally confirm voxelwise group-level statistics. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) appear to apply. Because only the abstract/metadata are available, fulltext_incomplete is set to true and confidence is moderate.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports group-level, voxelwise activation maps and within-group contrasts relevant to executive function. The working memory (W) task clearly falls within the executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports whole-brain acquisition and group statistical parametric maps (SPM t/Z maps) with voxelwise thresholding and presents within-group contrasts (W–C, T–C, T–W). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a Go/NoGo inhibition task (executive function: inhibition). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and multiple within-group task contrasts (false alarms–hits; correct rejections–hits; false alarms–correct rejections). Results are presented as voxelwise contrasts and interrogated with small-volume corrections but whole-brain voxelwise analyses are explicitly described, satisfying reporting via tables/figures/text. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This FDG-PET study uses a Stroop task (executive/inhibition domain) in schizophrenia patients and controls, but its analyses are ROI-based from limited slice sampling and do not report any group-level voxelwise task-evoked (within-group) activation maps or contrasts. Therefore it fails the whole-brain / voxelwise requirement and within-group task-contrast requirement. Exclusion ID met: E3 (only ROI analyses / no voxelwise results). Inclusion IDs met: I5 (PET task-based study), I6 (Stroop = inhibition/executive function), I9 (clinical participant groups reported). Inclusion IDs NOT met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map / whole-brain evidence), I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/attentional control over threat-related distractors (executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (voxel-wise comparisons with whole-brain correction and ROI small-volume corrections) and provides coordinates for activations. Key reported contrasts are within-group task contrasts (threat-related vs neutral distractor trials; start trials vs others) and regressions against state anxiety. Participants are healthy adults. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not report only ROI/SVC results (whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported), is not solely connectivity/resting analyses, includes within-group contrasts (not only between-group), and is empirical data (not a review). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control (task-switching/cognitive flexibility) with healthy adult participants. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (e.g., bivalent > univalent; switch > repetition) with thresholding and coordinates, and within-group contrasts are explicitly presented. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based Stroop paradigm (inhibition/cognitive control), reporting voxelwise, whole-brain group-level activation maps (incongruent vs congruent) for both patients and controls, and within-group contrasts. The methods explicitly describe voxel-by-voxel t-tests, voxelwise multiple regression, Talairach normalization, and tables/figures of activations. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function activations (I5–I10). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study with within-group voxelwise contrasts (MI vs LI) in healthy adults and reports results in-text and figures, the primary task is visual object categorization manipulated by stimulus impoverishment. While the authors interpret activations as reflecting top-down control and implicate working memory and attention, the fMRI task itself does not directly implement or manipulate a canonical executive-function domain listed in the inclusion criteria (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The explicit working-memory manipulation was behavioral (Experiment 2) and not a whole-brain fMRI task contrast. Therefore I6 (task within established executive function domains) is not satisfied, so the study does not meet all inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis.

This study reports task-based fMRI of executive function (2-back working memory) with clinical groups, employing voxelwise whole-brain analyses (voxelwise t-tests/ANOVAs) and reporting within-group task>fixation contrasts for each group. The paper provides complete methods, results, and discussion, and clearly describes clusterwise thresholding and voxelwise maps. All required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (fMRI executive task; working memory domain; voxelwise whole-brain analyses; within-group task contrasts reported; clinical participant groups included; results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not solely between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrast: decision > no-decision and group-average one-sample t-test), I9 (participant groups include clinical samples), I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I6 — task domain. The task is a modified Iowa Gambling Task probing decision-making and reward processing; the review requires tasks to fall within explicit executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although IGT involves aspects of decision-making and may engage executive processes, it is primarily a reward-based decision-making paradigm and is not clearly within the listed EF domains. Therefore it does not meet I6 and must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study that directly investigates response inhibition, an executive function (inhibition). Methods report whole-brain acquisition (contiguous slices covering entire brain) and voxelwise group analyses (one-sample t tests across 14 subjects) time-locked to lure (No-Go) events, constituting a within-group task contrast. Results are reported with cluster maps, figures, and Talairach coordinates (Table 1 and figures). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10.

This paper reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (object working memory) with healthy adult participants. The authors performed group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (SPM99), reporting within-group task contrasts (high vs low memory load; high vs low reward; interactions) with coordinates, tables and figures. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion requirements for fMRI task-based executive function, working memory domain, whole-brain voxelwise results, within-group contrasts, and permissible participant groups. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function) with event-related design. The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain GLM analyses (FDR-corrected), activation maps and Talairach coordinates, and explicit within-group task contrasts (delay-related maintenance activity examined within patients and controls, and correct vs. error trials). Participant groups include clinical (schizophrenia) and control samples. All required core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present, so the full text is complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study reports task-evoked whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses for cognitive tasks relevant to executive function. The Paced Auditory Serial Addition Test (PASAT) probes sustained attention, information processing speed, and working memory (an established executive domain); the study also included a recall (memory retrieval) task. The paper reports within-group one-sample SPM99 contrasts for patients and controls, between-group two-sample contrasts, multiple regression correlations with lesion load, and tables/figures of coordinate results — satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group task contrasts). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain). It reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (e.g., [Delay Forward 5 − Delay Forward 2] and [Delay Forward 5 − baseline]) and conducts a group-level SNGA second-level GLM (voxelwise whole-brain maps), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, and reports voxelwise group maps and coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of task activations in executive function.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of an executive function (working memory n-back). It reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (0-back vs fixation; 2-back vs 0-back) and group-level random-effects SPM analyses with whole-brain voxelwise results (tables, figures, cluster-corrected thresholds). The task falls within the executive domain (working memory). Results are presented as within-group and between-group voxelwise activation maps and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion, refs) is present. Therefore it satisfies I5–I10 and should be included.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of visual working memory (an executive function domain). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (group SDM and t-statistic maps), within-group task vs control contrasts, and presents maps and a table of local maxima. Participants are a within-group sample of 20 healthy adults. These satisfy inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables and references).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (N-back and item-recognition), which falls squarely within executive function domains. The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses (spatial F-maps, voxelwise ANOVAs) and within-group task contrasts (e.g., high vs low load; verbal vs nonverbal). Results include whole-brain voxelwise findings and coordinates reported in the text/tables. Participant group is healthy adults and within-group contrasts are provided. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of an antisaccade task (inhibition), which is an established executive function (inhibition). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level mixed-effects statistical parametric maps contrasting antisaccade vs prosaccade (within-group contrasts), includes tables of Talairach coordinates and figures of maps/time courses, and uses whole-voxel GLM/deconvolution rather than ROI-only analyses. Although imaging used limited axial slice coverage, the protocol and analyses are voxelwise and partial-brain acquisition is acceptable per criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual working memory (an executive function domain) using task-based maintenance vs manipulation contrasts. The authors report group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise GLM analyses (what vs where; maintenance vs manipulation), thresholded with FDR, with coordinates and figures/tables of activation. Within-group task contrasts are provided (e.g., maintenance vs manipulation, color vs spatial) for the healthy adult sample. Thus the study meets I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (working memory), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain group analyses — partial 16-slice coverage but voxelwise maps reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (within-group results in a participant group), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly examines short-term storage and comparison of auditory durations—a working memory operation within executive function. The paper reports a within-group contrast (discrimination minus identification) analyzed at the group level using voxelwise SPM99 procedures with whole-brain coverage, and presents voxel coordinates and activation figures/clusters. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable). Results and methods (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the full text provided. None of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical).
