This is an event-related fMRI study of prepulse inhibition (sensorimotor gating) and attentional modulation. It includes group-level voxelwise (pixel-by-pixel SPM/resampling) analyses and within-group contrasts (attended PPI vs ignored PPI vs startle-alone), and reports whole-slice voxelwise results. However, the task does not assess an established executive function domain as defined by the review (working memory, cognitive/response inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Prepulse inhibition reflects early sensorimotor gating and attentional modulation rather than higher-order executive control processes targeted in this meta-analysis. Therefore inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not met, while I7, I8, I9, and I10 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (delayed item recognition for letters) with a within-group, voxelwise second-level analysis. It tests WM load (set size) and reports whole-brain multivariate linear modeling and voxelwise GLM results (group-level), with figures and ROI follow-ups. The task clearly falls within the executive function domain (working memory). Results are presented as group-level voxelwise maps/plots (not ROI-only), and the contrast of task/delay versus implicit baseline and set-size effects are within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used task-based fMRI (modified PASAT) targeting executive/working-memory processes (I5,I6), reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps analyzed in SPM2 with FDR correction and figures/tables (I7,I10), and presents within-group task contrasts for the combined sample and separately for CFS and control groups (I8,I9). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that includes executive function tasks (working memory STERN; also attention and associative memory). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (e.g., NT vs CT for working memory; TO vs RS for attention; AL vs SC and RE vs SC for associative memory). Group-level voxelwise maps were generated by combining smoothed single-subject maps into group contrast maps (z-statistics) and results/ROIs with MNI coordinates are reported (Table 2); voxelwise SPM analyses (with FWE correction) were also performed. Participant sample is appropriate and full article provides methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of response inhibition (Go/NoGo), an established executive function (inhibition). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise group-level contrasts (NoGo vs Go) analyzed using SPM99 with random-effects one-sample t-tests, and presents whole-brain statistical parametric maps and stereotactic coordinates in tables/figures. These satisfy the requirement for whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results. Participants are a human sample (healthy adult males), and qualifying results are reported as coordinates and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study of a task that probes selective attention and spatial negative priming (inhibition). It meets inclusion: (I5) fMRI task-based study; (I6) addresses inhibition, an established executive function domain; (I7) reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-versus-rest statistical maps (P<0.05 corrected); (I8) includes within-group contrasts (task vs rest and condition comparisons within the same participant group); (I9) reports a within-group analysis in healthy adult participants; (I10) provides whole-brain results in figures and tables/coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Based on the abstract: this is an fMRI study of time perception and motor timing (rhythm perception), not tasks within established executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation), so it does not meet the review’s content requirement. I cannot verify group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses or within-group task contrasts from the provided text. Therefore I am excluding the study. No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 are clearly met given the limited information.

This is a task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (an executive function domain) using a within-subject emotional go/no-go paradigm. The paper reports voxelwise, random-effects whole-brain analyses (one-sample and paired-sample t tests) and regression analyses, with results described in tables and figures. At least one within-group task contrast is reported (e.g., positive distracter vs positive target; phase comparisons), and participant group (healthy premenopausal women) qualifies. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, refs).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that includes an established executive function paradigm (oculomotor delayed response — a spatial working memory task). Voxelwise, group-level and within-group task contrasts are reported (one-sample t-tests and voxelwise between-group t-tests; ODR vs visually guided saccade within-group contrasts are presented). Although acquisition had limited slice coverage, the analyses were voxelwise (whole-brain evidence criterion accepts partial-brain acquisition), and results are reported in figures and tables. therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (integration vs segregation) — an executive function domain. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects voxelwise ANOVAs and voxelwise conjunction contrasts), with within-group task contrasts (IN vs SG vs MO vs RO) and coordinates/tables/figures (Table 1, Figures). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Results are not limited to ROI or connectivity-only analyses. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control (stop-signal task) with healthy adults. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2) with family-wise error correction and coordinates for activations (group-level contrasts such as pre-SS vs pre-SE). The task falls within the executive function domain (inhibition). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly tests cognitive control/conflict and response inhibition during intentional false responding. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2 random-effects, FDR-corrected maps) and provides coordinate tables and figures for within-group contrasts (e.g., FALSE > TRUE, AUTO > NONAUTO). Healthy adult participants were tested and multiple within-group task contrasts are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the review are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back phonological and spatial tasks), which falls squarely within executive function domains. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2) with within-group contrasts (ON>OFF, PWM>SWM, SWM>PWM), conjunction analyses, and tables/figures with coordinates. Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported as voxelwise maps and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of working memory (an executive function) using a task-based Sternberg paradigm, meeting I5 and I6. The methods describe individual first-level contrasts (loads 5,7,9 modeled vs load 3 baseline) and group-level voxelwise analyses (including an all-subjects all-loads t-statistic map used to define ROIs), satisfying I7 and I8. Participant groups include patients, co-twins, and healthy controls (I9). Results and localization are reported in text/tables/figures consistent with I10. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only) and includes within-group task contrasts rather than only between-group contrasts. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This study reports task-based fMRI of a 2-back working memory task (an executive function domain). Methods describe whole-brain, voxelwise GLM and voxelwise ANOVAs, with task vs fixation (within-group) contrasts reported for each group and tables/figures of activation (coordinates). Participant groups include clinical samples (schizophrenia and siblings), which is allowed. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group activation contrasts are explicitly reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (span/listening span task) examining executive control resources. It reports whole-brain, group-level (random-effects) voxelwise analyses using SPM99, presents voxel coordinates and glass-brain figures (Table 2, Fig. 2), and reports within-group task contrasts (LST vs rest and LST vs Listen) including percentage signal changes and region correlations. Tasks clearly fall within executive function (working memory) domain. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using an auditory 2-back working memory task (executive function domain). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (multi-subject SPM99 maps with voxelwise thresholds and coordinates), and within-group task contrasts (task vs rest) for healthy participants. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

The study uses task-based fMRI and reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses (PLS) with within-group contrasts and coordinate tables, but the experimental task is episodic memory (encoding/recognition of unfamiliar faces), not an executive function or cognitive control task. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task study), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable), I10 (coordinates/results clearly reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (task does NOT fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails I6 (task domain mismatch).

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (unusual > canonical, canonical > unusual) and provides coordinates and figures, but the tasks are visual object categorization and recognition (with mental rotation and object-sensitive localizers). These tasks probe vision, object memory, and spatial transformation processes rather than established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although working memory and cognitive-control processes are discussed and localizers/secondary tasks are used, the primary experimental contrasts do not constitute core executive function tasks as defined by the review. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I5 and I6. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (within-group contrasts reported in healthy participants), I10 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive attention/control (Stroop variants) with group-level voxelwise activation maps comparing incongruent vs. neutral trials (a within-group task contrast). The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses, peak coordinates, and figures, and describes methods, subjects, and results (intro, methods, results, discussion present). Although acquisition used 15 slices (partial coverage), analyses were voxelwise and reported at the group level, which is acceptable per criteria. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports an fMRI, task-based investigation of stimulus–response incompatibility involving suppression of prepotent responses and working-memory demands, and reports within-group contrasts (task vs fixation; mixed vs compatible). Therefore I5, I6, I8, I9 and I10 are satisfied. However, the provided full text is incomplete (only title/abstract-level content available), so I cannot verify whether at least one group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analysis/map is reported (I7). Because I7 cannot be confirmed from the available content, the study cannot be included. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met based on available information.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) that reports group-level, voxelwise SPM contrasts (e.g., REP/REP CONT, MAT/MAT CONT, REP/MAT) with thresholded whole-brain maps and tables/figures. Although lower temporal/occipital lobes and cerebellum were not imaged (partial-brain coverage), the analyses are voxelwise and meet the meta-analysis’ allowance for partial coverage. Within-group task contrasts are reported and described in detail. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (only ROIs, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are triggered. Therefore the study meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an empirical PET meta-analysis that reanalyzes 63 subjects and 370 spatially normalized PET scans from nine task protocols using voxelwise SPM conjunction analysis. It includes within-group REST vs TASK contrasts (185 pairs of REST/TASK scans), reports whole-brain voxelwise results and stereotactic coordinates, and specifically addresses working memory and executive-function-related processes. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements: PET task-based paradigm (I5); contains tasks within executive domains (e.g., spatial working memory, manipulation/inhibition components) (I6); provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (I7); includes within-group task contrasts (I8); includes an eligible participant group (healthy adults) (I9); and reports whole-brain results/coordinates in text/tables (I10). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, event-related fMRI study that explicitly investigates cognitive control/conflict detection (ACC and PFC engagement) during a task (tip-of-the-tongue semantic retrieval) and interprets results in terms of conflict monitoring and retrieval control. The study reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses (cluster-corrected), includes within-group contrasts comparing TOT, know, and don’t-know trials, and uses a healthy adult participant group. Results are reported in the main text with ROI and voxelwise analyses. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This study reports an fMRI task-based investigation of sustained attention (Continuous Performance Test), which maps onto the executive domain of vigilance (I6). It includes healthy participants and reports a within-group task contrast (active CPT vs rest) analyzed at the group level using voxelwise SPM5 t-tests (P<0.001) with whole-brain coverage described in methods (I5, I7, I8, I9). Whole-brain results are described in the text and figures (I10). The paper is empirical and not excluded by any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or between-group-only contrasts). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using an n-back working memory paradigm (executive function domain). The full text reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (main effect of task reported with whole-brain FWE correction) as well as within-group contrasts (e.g., 2-back > 0-back and 0-back vs fixation) for both patients and controls. Partial reliance on small-volume correction for some DLPFC tests is present, but whole-brain voxelwise results are reported and tabulated. The methods, results, and discussion are complete in the provided full text. All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria are met.

Although this is an fMRI, task-based, whole-brain study that reports voxelwise within-group contrasts, the experimental manipulation targets semantic versus phonological language processing rather than established executive function or cognitive control domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails to meet I5 and I6 (does not assess executive function/cognitive control tasks). It does meet I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (healthy participant group reported), and I10 (whole-brain results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) with pre/post within-group task contrasts. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM99 normalization, voxel sampling, cluster correction) including a group-level Time x Task interaction as well as single-subject within-group contrasts; voxel coordinates and cluster-corrected results are reported. Participants are healthy adults (allowed). The full text includes introduction, methods, acquisition and analysis details, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back), an executive function. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (random-effects), including within-group task contrasts (e.g., 1-/2-/3-back vs 0-back; verbal vs spatial 3-back), with whole-brain voxelwise maps (cluster-corrected; coordinates reported). Although slice coverage omitted inferior temporal/cerebellar regions, partial-brain acquisition is allowed per criteria. Methods, results, and tables of coordinates are provided in the full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control (GO/NOGO), meeting executive-function domain criteria (inhibition). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests, voxelwise thresholding with cluster-correction), and presents within-group task contrasts (event-related Stops vs baseline and Fast vs Slow conditions). Participants are healthy adults; results are reported in figures and tables with cluster coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment of criteria.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of working memory (n-back), an established executive function domain, using whole-brain BOLD acquisition and voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM99, one-sample t-tests to create group maps and ANOVA). Within-group task contrasts (WM vs 0-Back) are reported for the two participant groups (young and elderly). Results are presented as voxelwise group maps and described in the text, with supplementary ROI post-hoc analyses. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based N-back working-memory paradigm in postmenopausal women. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (3-back > 0-back) with SPM2, corrected p-values and MNI coordinates/cluster extents, satisfying requirement for a within-group task contrast and whole-brain activation maps. The task falls within executive function (working memory) and participant group is acceptable. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study should be included for meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI study that includes a working-memory (n-back) manipulation, which is an established executive function domain. The paper reports within-group, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., high > low WM load) analyzed with whole-brain random-effects GLM, provides coordinates and thresholded maps, and describes results in text and tables. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study probing top-down attentional control (dynamic ‘zooming in’/‘zooming out’ of attention), which the authors frame as a cognitive control/top–down attentional control process. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (SPM2) with cluster-corrected thresholds and tables/figures of coordinates. Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., zooming in > HLB, zooming out > HLB, in > out), satisfying the requirement for within-group task contrasts. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable sample). The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI task-based study of motor response inhibition (Go/NoGo) in manic bipolar patients. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM99) and provides within-group contrasts (correct NoGo minus correct Go) for both patients and controls, with coordinates and cluster-level inference. The task maps to the executive domain of inhibition. Results are reported in the main text with MNI/Talairach coordinates. No exclusion criteria are violated (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that investigates antisaccade (inhibition) and visually guided saccade performance. It falls squarely within the executive function domain of inhibition. The methods report voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects analyses (SPM99), present statistical parametric maps and tables of coordinates for group-level within-group contrasts (saccade vs control; antisaccade vs control; antisaccade vs saccade). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy volunteers. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and references, and appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a rule-based go/nogo (ocular baseball) task that directly probes executive functions—specifically inhibition and rule-guided decision-making. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain analyses (individual subject contrasts and group-level SPM99 analyses with voxelwise thresholds and cluster extent) and provides coordinates and figures for activations (e.g., right VLPFC, SPL, FEF, SEF). Tasks fall within established executive domains (inhibition/rule processing). Participants are healthy adults and within-group contrasts (decided-nogo vs always-nogo; decided-go vs always-go) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment of criteria. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and none of the exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that probes nonspatial attention shifting—a form of cognitive flexibility (executive function). It reports voxelwise, group-level contrasts (e.g., shifting attention vs sustained attention) with stereotactic normalization and reproducible activation foci (tables of coordinates and reproducibility maps). Within-group task contrasts are presented (shifting vs sustained; sustained vs fixation). Participants are healthy adults. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) with within-group task contrasts and voxelwise/voxel-based analyses reported (including group-average activation maps in supplementary material). The paper reports task-evoked haemodynamic responses across encoding, maintenance and retrieval phases, domain (verbal vs spatial) effects, and group-level comparisons; results are presented in text, figures and supplementary material. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The provided content appears to be only an abstract-level summary (full text incomplete). From this text we can verify I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function) and I6 (working memory domain). The report describes a within-group comparison between Item and Order tasks, supporting I8, and a participant sample is implied (I9). However, the abstract does not provide enough information to confirm I7 (presence of a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical map) or I10 (format of whole-brain results such as coordinates or clear voxelwise maps). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) are clearly met based on the abstract alone. Because key inclusion criteria (I7 and I10) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, I exclude this record pending the complete article.

This study reports fMRI and EEG investigations of a working memory (face delayed recognition) task (meeting I5 and I6), includes within-group task contrasts and group-level behavioral/statistical analyses (I8, I9). However, the manuscript does not present a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation map; fMRI analyses are described in terms of individual-subject ROI localization and ROI-based time-course analyses rather than reporting group-level voxelwise statistical maps. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI-style analyses reported with no voxelwise group map). Full text appears complete. Excluded on basis of E3; inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9; inclusion criteria not met: I7.

This is an empirical fMRI study of verbal working memory (Sternberg paradigm), which qualifies as an executive function task. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level random-effects analyses using SPM99 (linear and quadratic load contrasts and load 6 vs. 2), and presents voxelwise results in figures and tables of coordinates. At least one within-group task contrast is reported. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

Full text is paywalled and only abstract/metadata are available. The abstract confirms an fMRI study of a 1-back verbal working memory task in Alzheimer’s patients and controls, so I5 (fMRI task), I6 (working memory domain), and I9 (participant groups including clinical sample) appear satisfied. However, I cannot verify whether voxelwise whole-brain group-level maps or at least one WITHIN-GROUP task contrast are reported (the abstract emphasizes between-group comparisons). Therefore I7 (whole-brain voxelwise evidence), I8 (within-group task contrast), and I10 (clear reporting of whole-brain results) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be confidently applied based on available content. Because the full article is not available, inclusion cannot be confirmed—obtain the full text to reassess.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based working memory (Sternberg Item Recognition Paradigm) paradigm, which falls squarely within executive function. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise statistical maps for both schizophrenic and normal groups (e.g., 5-target vs Arrows; 5t vs 2t), describes group-averaged voxelwise analyses in Talairach space, and applies whole-brain thresholds (stringent p-values for non a priori regions). Although slice coverage may be limited, the analysis is voxelwise and thus meets the partial-brain allowance. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical work) are met. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This study reports task-based fMRI of working memory (modified Sternberg), with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects maps; tables of coordinates and figures), and within-group task contrasts (e.g., maintenance-retrieval vs rest and first vs last retrieval sections; parametric modulation of exponential signal change). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps and coordinates. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for fMRI executive-function activation studies.

This paper reports an empirical task-based fMRI study using the PASAT (a working-memory/executive function task) in patients (CISSMS) and matched healthy controls. Methods describe whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects group analyses (SPM99), with within-group one-sample t-tests (task vs control) and between-group contrasts; results include regional activations and correlations. Although EPI acquisition used 17 slices (partial coverage), analyses were voxelwise and therefore satisfy the meta-analysis allowance for partial-brain studies. The study provides within-group task contrasts for at least one group (controls and patients) and reports whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/results in text/figures/tables. All inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study (SPM2) with group-level, voxelwise analyses and whole-brain coverage reporting peak coordinate tables. The task explicitly probes executive domains relevant to the review (action planning, monitoring/vigilance, rule processing, initiation/stopping), and reports within-group contrasts (e.g., action planning > coasting, monitoring traffic > coasting, traffic rules > coasting). Results are reported as voxelwise group t-tests with coordinates (Tables), satisfying reporting requirements. Participants are a within-group adult sample (licensed taxi drivers). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion, tables) is provided. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based, within-subject event-related fMRI study that reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (mixed-model ANOVAs) with tabulated activation coordinates and cluster thresholds. The task requires encoding and short-term maintenance of interval durations and making duration comparisons, engaging working memory, auditory rehearsal, and decision-making (executive) processes; the authors explicitly analyze working-memory/decision (difficulty) contrasts. Thus the study meets the meta-analysis focus on executive-function domains (working memory/decision processes), provides within-group task contrasts (encoding vs baseline; hard vs easy discriminations), reports voxelwise whole-brain results in tables/figures, and uses a healthy adult participant group. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function domain) using an event-related Sternberg paradigm in premanifest Huntington’s disease and matched controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM5) including within-group one-sample t-tests for ICA-derived task-related components and provides stereotaxic coordinates and statistical thresholds. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (working memory), I7 (group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts/maps), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (coordinates/results clearly described). The study is empirical, not ROI-only, and not limited to connectivity-only analyses (it reports task-evoked spatial ICA components and voxelwise maps), so no exclusion criteria apply (E3–E6 not met). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical human fMRI study using task-based paradigms that probe categorization with a delayed match-to-sample (DMS) design that requires stimulus maintenance and comparison. The tasks implicate working memory/executive processing (authors explicitly interpret categorization as involving working memory), and the manuscript reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (CAT vs AUD, CAT vs Rest, AUD vs Rest) using SPM random-effects group analyses, figures, and tables of MNI/Talairach coordinates. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (random-effects, cluster thresholds) despite limited slice coverage (22 slices); partial-brain acquisition is allowable per inclusion rules. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Results are reported as group-level activation maps and coordinate tables. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports task-based fMRI of working memory (auditory digital WM) in healthy volunteers, but it does not provide a group-level, voxelwise statistical activation map. Methods indicate limited slice coverage (four-plane slices) and the group-level analysis is described as regions-of-interest analyzed with the McNemar test rather than voxelwise statistics; results are reported as images and descriptions of activated regions rather than as voxelwise group maps or coordinates. Therefore it fails the requirement for a group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map and appears to report ROI-based group analyses only. Exclusion is based on E3 (only ROI analyses/no voxelwise group results).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of mental calculation that probes cognitive processes including working memory and rule-based manipulation (executive functions). The study reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (fixed-effects), multiple within-group task contrasts (each condition vs result-matching baseline; direct condition comparisons), and whole-brain activation maps/tables in the text and figures. Participants are healthy adults. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI of executive-function domains and provides within-group, voxelwise task-evoked results suitable for inclusion.

The paper is excluded because it does not provide qualifying whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked fMRI results required by the review. Although the study uses fMRI to localize left DLPFC and employs a task (reading span test) that falls within the working memory (executive) domain, the fMRI data appear to be used only for per-subject localization (and the main experiment is a TMS behavioral disruption). No group-level voxelwise activation map or clearly reported within-group task contrast at the group level is described in the full text. Thus exclusion criterion E3 applies (reporting only ROI/localizing results without voxelwise group results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI used with a task) and I6 (task = working memory). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise task map) and I8 (no clear within-group voxelwise task contrast reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive set-shifting (executive function: cognitive flexibility). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects GLM; FDR-corrected maps), multiple within-group task contrasts (shift, generate, update, maintenance), and results presented in tables/figures. Participants are healthy volunteers (within-group contrasts reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references, so the full text appears complete.

This is a task-based PET study of verbal working memory (an executive function), reporting within-group contrasts (2-back WM vs control) and whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM96 with reported activated/deactivated regions (Brodmann areas and cluster thresholds). Participants are healthy volunteers. The manuscript provides methods, results, and discussion describing voxelwise task-evoked activation maps, satisfying all inclusion criteria and violating no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory/executive function in an elderly sample. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (voxel-level threshold P<0.001 uncorrected) and whole-brain activation results (tables/figures) for within-group task contrasts (read+memory and recognition phases vs baseline). Tasks fall within the working memory/executive function domain. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria. The study is appropriate for pooling executive-function task activations across participant groups in the meta-analysis.

The study is an fMRI task-based investigation of working memory (an executive function) with within-group task vs control contrasts, and reports voxelwise activation coordinates. However, the paper does not clearly present a group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map (I7). Analyses are described as voxelwise at the individual-subject level with reported per-subject peaks and averaged coordinates, but no explicit group-level voxelwise statistical map is reported. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I7, so it must be excluded. The full text appears complete.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). The study is a PET task-based study with an active vigilance task, so it meets I5 (PET task-based), I6 (vigilance is an executive domain), I8 (within-group activation reported for patients during the vigilance task) and I9 (clinical participant group allowed). However, the abstract does not explicitly confirm that at least one group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map was reported (I7). Because I7 cannot be verified from the provided content and full text is incomplete, I cannot confirm all inclusion criteria are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met. Recommend obtaining full text to confirm voxelwise whole-brain analyses before including.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study with group-level voxelwise maps and within-group contrasts, but the tasks (lexicosemantic decision, tone discrimination, and visuomotor sequence learning) do not target established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails the core inclusion criteria I5 and I6 required for a meta-analysis of executive function activations. It does meet criteria for whole-brain voxelwise analysis and within-group contrasts, and participant sampling is acceptable, but the cognitive domains assessed are outside the review scope.

The study is an fMRI event-related item-recognition (verbal working memory) task, so it clearly meets I5 (task-based fMRI) and I6 (working memory). However the provided full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata). The abstract mentions linear regression to locate activation and subsequent ROI analyses but does not explicitly confirm a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation map (I7) nor explicitly report a within-group task contrast (I8). Because ALL inclusion criteria must be verifiable and I7 and I8 cannot be confirmed from the incomplete text, I exclude the study. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met based on available information.

This is an empirical PET study using task-based activation (H2(15)O PET) that directly tests an executive function (counting Stroop — cognitive control/inhibition). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level SPM99 analyses contrasting incongruent vs. neutral conditions (a within-group task contrast), and it includes both whole-brain analyses and ROI/small-volume-corrected results with coordinates and tables reported. Participants are a defined group of healthy volunteers. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that reports voxelwise, group-level task-evoked activation maps (SPM analyses) and within-group contrasts (task vs rest and task comparisons). The PHONO task explicitly engages phonological working memory (phonological loop) and the PUZZLE task requires visuospatial manipulation and motor executive processes, which fall within executive-function domains (working memory / planning/manipulation). Although slice coverage was partial, analyses were voxelwise and therefore qualify under whole-brain evidence criteria. Results are reported in the main text with activation maps and quantitative comparisons across tasks. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and sufficient for screening.

This is an event-related task fMRI study of working memory (spatial vs. object) with within-group task contrasts and appropriate task-based design. However, all analyses were performed using regions-of-interest (caudate nucleus, DLPFC, M1, PPC) and group analyses extracted ROI-based t-values rather than reporting a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical map. The manuscript explicitly states that all analyses were performed with ROIs and used ROI-based correction, and group tests collapsed across voxels within ROIs. Therefore it does not provide the required group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (I7 not met) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control using a stop-signal (inhibition) paradigm in healthy adults. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (SPM2) with family-wise error correction and provides voxel coordinates and contrasts (e.g., SE vs. SS, SS vs. G, pSE vs. pG), satisfying within-group task contrasts. Results are reported across the whole brain (including thalamus, ACC, SMA, etc.). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and conclusions. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical PET study that used a task-based immediate serial recall paradigm probing working memory (an executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (whole-brain normalization, smoothing, voxelwise contrasts and thresholding) and provides within-group task contrasts (e.g., main effect of working memory, irrelevant speech contrasts, and interaction contrasts). Coordinates and statistic peaks are reported. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports task-based fMRI (and EEG) of an executive function task (intradimensional/extradimensional rule shifts; cognitive flexibility). It includes within-group, voxelwise whole-brain group-level contrasts (negative>positive feedback for ID and ED conditions) analyzed with SPM2 and reported with coordinates and cluster results. The task falls within executive function/cognitive control (cognitive flexibility), and whole-brain voxelwise analyses and ROI analyses are described. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of task-evoked executive function activations. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables/figures) is provided and appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (2-back CPT) in healthy adults, reporting voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses contrasting 2-back vs 0-back (a within-group task contrast). Results include coordinates and cluster statistics (BA10) and methods indicate whole-brain voxelwise analysis. Thus the paper meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of a two-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). The paper reports within-group, epoch-related GLM contrasts (task vs rest) and presents group-level voxelwise SPM results (figures and tables of activations/deactivations), satisfying whole-brain, task-evoked map requirements. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable sample). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (image acquisition, GLM), Results (voxelwise activations, tables, figures) and Discussion, so the article is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are violated. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study investigating inhibition of return (an inhibitory attentional effect). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses (random-effects ANOVA; cluster-level correction) with standard within-group task contrasts (e.g., Long_SOA (Cued+Uncued) > Short_SOA; cued vs uncued), and provides coordinates/tables and figures. Participants are healthy adults. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore it meets I5–I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Full text is incomplete (HTML skeleton only). Title and metadata indicate an event-related fMRI study of context processing in dorsolateral prefrontal cortex in patients with schizophrenia, so I5 (fMRI task-based study) and I6 (executive-function domain: context processing/working memory) appear met. However core article content (methods, results) is missing, so critical inclusion criteria cannot be verified: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map) cannot be confirmed, I8 (within-group task contrast) cannot be confirmed, I9 (while participants are clinical, within-group contrast reporting cannot be verified) and I10 (reporting of whole-brain results in coordinates/figures/text) cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) are demonstrably met from the incomplete content. Because the full text is incomplete and key inclusion criteria cannot be verified, the study is excluded pending a complete full text.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of interference resolution and working memory (executive control). It reports task-based within-group voxelwise contrasts (interference vs control) at the group level with whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses and tables of stereotaxic coordinates. The tasks fall squarely within executive-function domains (working memory/inhibition). Partial slice coverage is acceptable per criteria and voxelwise group contrasts are provided and described in text/tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present, so fulltext is complete.

This is a PET study with whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99) comparing syntactically complex (SO) versus simple (OS) sentences within groups; coordinates and within-group contrasts are reported. However, the study’s primary focus is language/syntactic processing and individual differences in working memory and processing speed, not an executive function or cognitive control task per se. Although working memory was measured as an individual-difference variable, the experimental task is a plausibility judgment for sentence comprehension rather than a task designed to probe established executive domains (working memory task paradigms, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I5 and I6. Inclusion criteria met: I7, I8, I9, I10. Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that investigates internal initiation/modulation of externally cued motor sequences. It meets inclusion: (I5) uses fMRI and assesses cognitive control aspects (internal initiation/modulation), (I6) examines initiation/internal pacing (an accepted executive domain here), (I7) reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level SPM analyses, (I8) includes within-group task contrasts (e.g., task vs baseline and condition contrasts like TATA vs 1 Hz), (I9) uses a participant group (healthy volunteers) and reports within-group results, (I10) whole-brain results are described in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore include.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study probing working memory and selective attention (executive-function domains). The methods describe voxelwise, group-level statistical maps (NT–CT and TO–RS contrasts), normalization to CMNI and thresholded z-statistics, and tables/figures of activation — satisfying whole-brain, voxelwise reporting. Within-group task contrasts are computed and used to generate group maps (i.e., task > control/rest contrasts), and results are reported in text/tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly investigates cognitive control/conflict (processing of semantic–prosodic incongruence) using a within-group, voxelwise whole-brain analysis. Group-level random-effects SPM2 contrasts are reported (e.g., CONF vs NOCONF, main effect vs baseline), with whole-brain correction and voxelwise inference. The paradigm requires overriding task-irrelevant semantic information to identify prosody (inhibition/response selection), which maps onto executive function domains. Participants are healthy adults and within-group contrasts are provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusions) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Exclusion E3 met: the paper uses an ROI-based analysis pipeline (voxels were selected within anatomically defined ROIs based on a per-subject main effect of time and subsequent ROI-averaged time-course ANOVAs) and the main reported results are ROI-averaged time courses and across-subject ROI statistics. The manuscript does not present a group-level, voxelwise task-activation statistical map (i.e. no whole-group voxelwise contrast/SPM-style maps are reported), so criterion I7 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked map) is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study of cognitive control), I6 (task involves inhibition/countermanding), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported, e.g. STOP vs GO, STOP-success vs STOP-fail), I9 (within-group healthy volunteer sample reported), I10 (task activation results are described in text/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise task map reported).

This is an empirical fMRI study that (1) uses a verbal working memory task (an established executive function domain) and reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (verbal working memory > rest). The paper provides whole-brain, spatially normalized voxelwise analyses, a within-group task contrast, and reports results from healthy participant groups; results are described in detail across methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the review are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using an executive-function task (two-back working memory) and reports within-group task vs fixation measures, so it meets I5, I6, I8, and I9. However, the paper’s analyses are focused on thalamic ROI-based task activation measures and do not present any group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps in this full text (the authors note whole-brain exploratory analyses were published elsewhere). Therefore it fails I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses reported with no voxelwise results in this article). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Excluded because study reports only ROI/SVC-based analyses rather than presenting a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map (Exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study of cognitive tasks), I6 (includes an executive-domain task: working memory), I8 (within-group task contrasts were computed), I9 (healthy adult participant group). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is reported; analyses are restricted to pre-defined ROIs with small-volume correction). I10: reporting of whole-brain voxelwise results as coordinates/figures is not evident in the full text provided. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded under E3.

This is a task-based PET study using FDG with a numerical calculation paradigm and reports group-level, voxelwise SPM contrasts (task vs baseline) showing task-evoked activations. Numerical calculations engage working memory/executive processes and elicited prefrontal activation, satisfying the review’s executive-function domain requirement. The paper includes whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM) and within-group task contrasts; results are reported in text, figures, and tables. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that manipulates the central executive component of working memory using a number-subtraction task (meets I5). The task targets working memory/central executive executive-domain processes (meets I6). Imaging methods and analyses are whole-brain and voxelwise (SPM99 preprocessing, normalization, second-level random-effects one-sample t tests with voxelwise thresholds and cluster extent), and coordinates/figures/tables of activations are reported (meets I7 and I10). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (each subtraction condition vs baseline; high-demand vs low-demand; interaction contrasts) at group level (meets I8). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults (meets I9). No exclusion criteria are violated (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive control/dual-task processing in healthy adults. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-head analyses (e.g., DM>SM, SM>SP), Time×Group and Time×Group×Condition interactions, and provides coordinates and statistical maps in the text/tables. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Based on the abstract, this is an fMRI task study addressing cognitive processing with a contrast between two motor tasks differing in sustained attention, so I5 (fMRI task study), I6 (task involves vigilance/sustained attention), I8 (within-group task contrast) and I9 (any participant group — within-group contrast reported) appear to be satisfied. However, I cannot verify I7 (presence of a group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map) or I10 (acceptable whole-brain reporting in coordinates/figures/text) from the provided material. No exclusion criteria are clearly met (e.g., not clearly methods-only or ROI-only). Because critical inclusion criteria (I7 and I10) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, I exclude the study pending full-text availability.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports within-group, whole-brain voxelwise activation contrasts for reasoning tasks. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task-based study assessing cognitive control/executive processes — reasoning tasks engage executive processes), I6 (tasks involve maintenance and manipulation of information consistent with the working memory/executive domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses with group-level reporting of activated ROIs and Talairach coordinates), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported: conditional vs baseline, relational vs baseline, conditional vs relational), I9 (healthy adult participant group; within-group contrasts reported), I10 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates and Z-scores in text/tables/figures). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

Exclusion criteria met: E4 (study reports only connectivity/resting-state analyses without reporting a task-evoked voxelwise activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study including a task paradigm) and I6 (task = working memory, an established executive function domain). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is reported), I8 (no within-group task contrast voxelwise activation map is presented; analyses focus on connectivity differences between rest and a continuous 2-back task rather than task-evoked activation maps), and I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise task activation coordinates or maps reported for a within-group task contrast). The full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it only reports connectivity/resting-state analyses and does not provide the required task activation maps or within-group voxelwise contrasts required for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation contrasts for within-group task comparisons. Although the primary focus is implicit sequence learning, the authors explicitly interpret activations in terms of spatial working memory and response monitoring (executive/cognitive control processes). The study used voxelwise SPM analyses with cluster-level correction across the entire brain, and contrasts compare fixed-sequence vs random-order blocks (within-group). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported in figures and tables. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a visual oddball paradigm that probes attention/vigilance and working memory (rehearsal/counting) — both established executive function domains. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain (near full coverage) activation maps and presents within-group task contrasts for low-risk and high-risk groups (task vs implicit baseline), with statistical maps and corrected results described in the text. Although a small portion of orbital frontal and anterior inferior temporal lobes were not imaged, the analysis was voxelwise and permutation-based, satisfying whole-brain (voxelwise) reporting. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses are reported (e.g., manipulation vs maintenance, high vs low load) with statistical maps and tables; within-group contrasts are explicitly presented. Results are reported in tables and figures and described in the text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

Only the title and abstract (metadata) are provided; full article (methods, results, figures/tables) is not available, so key inclusion criteria cannot be verified. Inclusion criteria met based on abstract: I5 (event-related fMRI assessing working memory, an executive function) and I6 (task falls within executive function domain: working memory). Inclusion criteria not verifiable from provided content: I7 (cannot confirm a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map is reported), I8 (cannot confirm a within-group task contrast is reported at group level), I10 (cannot confirm whole-brain results are reported as voxelwise maps or coordinates in text/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met from the abstract. Because essential methodological/results details are missing, I exclude this record pending full text access.

This study is excluded because it reports ROI-based analyses only and does not provide group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (exclusion E3). Meets inclusion: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function — Stroop, Go/No-Go, Sternberg), I6 (tasks fall within executive domains: inhibition and working memory), I8 (within-group task contrasts were computed at first level: NoGo vs Go, Incongruent vs Congruent, Retain6 vs Retain2, Finger tapping vs fixation), I9 (healthy participant group reported). Does NOT meet inclusion I7: no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation maps are reported — analyses are ROI summaries and paired ROI tests; and thus there are no voxelwise group maps or reported coordinates/figures that would qualify per I7. I10 (acceptable formats) is not applicable as no whole-brain voxelwise results were reported. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, within-group task contrasts of an imitation paradigm (COPY vs INCONGRUOUS, COPY vs SPATIAL) in healthy participants and reports voxelwise results with coordinates. However, the experimental task assesses perception–action matching / imitation (social sensorimotor processes) rather than an established executive function domain. Although the authors discuss working memory and error-detection processes, the tasks do not constitute classical executive-function paradigms (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation) as required by the review inclusion criteria. Therefore I5 and I6 are not satisfied, while I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a Stroop task to probe attentional control/executive function (inhibition/selection). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, mixed-effects group analyses (FLAME) with whole-brain cluster-based inference and tables of peak coordinates for contrasts (e.g., incongruent vs neutral; one-word vs four-word). Tasks clearly fall within executive function domains (inhibition/cognitive control). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is a task-based fMRI study using a 2-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses were reported (random-effects SPM2 analyses with FDR-corrected thresholds and coordinates/ROIs reported). Within-group task contrasts (task vs baseline and condition comparisons: Word, Cross, Within) are presented. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so core content is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This is an empirical PET study reporting task-based activation during executive/cognitive tasks (WCST and RPM). It includes within-group, voxelwise group-level contrasts (task minus control) using SPM and voxel-by-voxel analyses, with whole-brain coverage and reported statistical maps/tables. WCST is a canonical executive function (working memory/cognitive flexibility) satisfying the executive-domain requirement. Results are presented as group-level activation maps and tables/figures, and full methods, results, and discussion are provided in the full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts). Full text appears complete.

Although this is an fMRI task study of sustained attention/pain (meets I5, I6) and it reports within-group task contrasts (no-pain vs pain/CPT conditions) in both healthy and OA groups (meets I8 and I9) with results described in the text/figures (meets I10), the analyses are confined to a hand-drawn anterior cingulate ROI. The paper does not present a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain (or partial-brain voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map outside an a priori ROI; the reported results are ROI-focused/IC-weightings within the cingulate. This constitutes an ROI-only analysis with no voxelwise, group-level activation map reported, triggering exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criterion I7 (group-level voxelwise task map) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (executive function). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The study reports voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses (SPM2) with within-group task contrasts (3-back vs OFF) and provides tables/figures with coordinates. Participant sample (healthy male social drinkers) is acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a verbal Sternberg working memory task (an executive function—working memory). It reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level analyses (FSL FEAT/FLAME) including contrasts of WM>rest and parametric linear [−1 0 1] and nonlinear [−1 2 −1] load-dependent effects, with whole-brain coverage and cluster-thresholded Z maps. Results are reported for children, adolescents, and young adults (within-group contrasts present for each). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and include within-group activation contrasts (not only between-group). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of visual working memory (an executive function: working memory) in healthy adults. The authors ran group-level voxelwise SPM analyses (e.g., a significant Task > fixation effect, P < 0.05 corrected) to identify ROIs and report within-group task contrasts and load/feature effects across the sample. Whole-brain coverage (except the bottom of the cerebellum) and voxelwise results are described in the methods and results. Thus the study meets I5 (fMRI task-based executive function), I6 (working memory domain), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group reported), and I10 (whole-brain results described). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (2-back vs 0-back) in healthy adults. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level random-effects analyses (2-back minus 0-back) and interaction contrasts, with whole-brain voxelwise results presented as statistical maps and coordinates. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations (working memory). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an event-related fMRI study using a task-based arithmetic verification paradigm that probes cognitive control/working memory and interference resolution (executive functions). The study reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM99) contrasting incorrect vs. correct equations (a within-group task contrast), with whole-brain coverage and results presented as significant clusters/figures/tables. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy subjects. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI with voxelwise whole-brain analyses and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract we can confirm: I5 (PET, task-based WCST), I6 (task is an executive function — WCST), I8 (within-group task contrast: WCST vs sensorimotor control), and I9 (participant groups, including patient and controls). However I7 (requirement for a group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical map) cannot be verified from the available text, nor can I10 (clear reporting of whole-brain results in coordinates/figures/text). Because the full text is missing, I cannot determine whether analyses were voxelwise whole-brain or ROI-based (potential E3). Per screening rules, inability to verify required inclusion criteria (I7) and potential violation of E3 mandates exclusion. No exclusion criteria are explicitly met based on the abstract alone. Recommend obtaining full text to reassess.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain task contrasts relevant to executive function. The tasks include spatial working memory (an established executive function domain) and sustained spatial attention/vigilance. The paper presents group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM), reports coordinates and statistical maps for contrasts such as WM delay vs control and attention delay vs control, and performs laterality contrasts (attend-right vs attend-left). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory and vigilance domains), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses and coordinates reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (healthy adult participant group within-group contrasts reported), and I10 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates and described in text). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory updating (executive function) with healthy adult participants. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Group-level, voxelwise task activation contrasts are reported (e.g., all-updates > hold; RULE > NMBR; NMBR > RULE) with whole-brain voxelwise thresholding and cluster correction; supplemental tables/coordinates are available. Analyses are within-group task contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based operation span paradigm targeting verbal working memory and the central executive (executive function). The study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with voxel- and cluster-level thresholds, provides within-group task contrasts (Concrete vs Abstract OST phases and task vs baseline), and reports coordinates/figures. Participants are healthy adults and the full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical PET task-based study that explicitly probes spatial working memory and planning during covered maze traversal, which fall within executive function domains (working memory/planning). The study reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., covered vs motor, covered vs visual, covered vs uncovered), with stereotactic coordinates and SPM{Z} maps described in the text. Participants (healthy adults) are a qualifying group and whole-brain results are reported in coordinates/tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study examining cognitive control/executive function (representation and maintenance of context, selection) during a missing-letter language production task. Inclusion criteria: I5 satisfied—uses fMRI and assesses cognitive control; I6 satisfied—task engages working memory/maintenance and selection (working memory domain of executive function); I7 satisfied—reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects GLM, AFNI; reported whole-brain activation maps/coordinates); I8 satisfied—reports within-group task contrasts (context vs neutral; context-appropriate vs context-inappropriate; selection demand contrasts); I9 satisfied—within-group contrasts on healthy adult participants; I10 satisfied—whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly tests deception (pretending to know) which requires intentional response manipulation and cognitive control, consistent with executive function/inhibition domains. The study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2; random-effects ANOVA) with coordinates and thresholding, and presents within-group task contrasts (e.g., Lie vs Truth, LN vs CR, FR vs CR). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Results are reported as voxelwise activation maps and peak coordinates in the text/tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) comparing individuals with schizophrenia and controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (task–fixation and onset-transient correlations), and presents within-group task contrasts and regional time courses for each group. Tasks include working memory (2-back), encoding, and recognition — all within executive/cognitive domains. Whole-brain coverage and voxelwise analyses are described; results are reported in figures, tables, and text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10.
