Participant sample (clinical OCD and healthy controls) is acceptable per criteria. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is provided, allowing extraction of whole-brain task activation coordinates. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (letter vs visuospatial decision tasks) in healthy participants. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts with coordinates and corrected statistics (task vs baseline and task vs task), satisfying within-group task contrasts. Tasks probe executive processes (response selection, inhibition, conflict monitoring), and results are reported as coordinates/figures. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical neuroimaging research. Full text appears to include introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (syllable working memory) in healthy Japanese adults. It assesses an executive function domain (working memory) using block-designed task contrasts and reports within-group voxelwise analyses (task vs rest and l/r vs b/n or d/n) using SPM99, with activation maps and coordinate tables provided. Thus it provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, figures/tables, references).

This fMRI study reports within-group, voxelwise task contrasts (game > dot, game > scene, game > random) assessing working memory and recognition tasks in chess players — the game > dot contrast isolates working-memory/executive processes. Whole-brain images were acquired and SPM99 voxelwise group-level maps (corrected p<.05) and activation foci are reported. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for task-based fMRI of executive function with whole-brain, within-group voxelwise contrasts. Although the group analysis used a fixed-effects model and the sample is small (n=5), the inclusion criteria do not exclude fixed-effects or small samples. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using verbal and non-verbal working memory tasks (executive function domain: working memory). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise working-memory versus baseline contrasts, group-level whole-brain t maps, voxelwise regression with PCS scores, and VOI analyses. Participants include concussed athletes and control athletes (clinical and healthy groups). Whole-brain, group-level statistical maps are described and displayed; analyses are voxelwise rather than ROI-only. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10), and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM) and coordinates, including within-group contrasts (main effect of condition, main effect of velocity, regression analyses). Although the primary paradigm probes smooth pursuit eye movements, the contrast of target blanking versus continuous presentation was explicitly designed to engage extraretinal mechanisms such as prediction, monitoring and short-/mid-term spatial working memory (DLPFC, angular gyrus)—functions within established executive domains (working memory/monitoring). Participants were healthy adults and results are reported as group-level voxelwise maps with tables of coordinates. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI task-based study of verbal working memory (an executive function domain). It reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (e.g., maintenance vs control; words vs pseudowords; 5 vs 2 load), including random-effects one-sample t tests and whole-brain functional connectivity, and provides sufficient methods, results, and discussion in the full text. Participants are a within-group healthy sample. Reporting includes voxelwise maps and contrasts described in text and supplemental materials. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (working memory span/dual-task coordination) with healthy adult participants. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (random-effects group analyses and t-tests), within-group task contrasts (e.g., Read+Remember vs Read; Read+Remember vs Remember), and reports whole-brain activations with coordinates and tables. Although slice coverage is limited in Experiment 1, the analyses are voxelwise and whole-brain contrasts are presented; results are reported in text, figures, and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a modified Wisconsin Card Sorting Test (set-shifting) that targets cognitive flexibility — an executive function. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM99 random-effects GLM) with multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., A minus D, A minus B, B minus C) and provides Talairach/MNI coordinates and statistical maps. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Reporting includes tables, figures, methods, results, and discussion, satisfying whole-text completeness. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for pooling executive-function task activations.

This fMRI study includes a classic executive-function task (Stroop; inhibition domain) and a task-based moral-dilemma paradigm. Group-level, voxelwise analyses are reported (ICA-derived spatial maps, voxelwise paired-samples t tests, and tables of coordinates/cluster statistics are provided), and within-group task contrasts (task vs rest/fixation and task-condition contrasts) are described. Whole-brain voxelwise results and coordinates are reported in tables and supplemental materials. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI (within-group contrasts, whole-brain voxelwise maps, coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive function/cognitive control (time-estimation feedback and Stroop tasks). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (contrasts such as incongruent>congruent and errors>correct in the Stroop task; feedback contrasts in the time-estimation task) with figures/tables, and at least one within-group task contrast. Participant group is healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Although slice coverage was limited to 28 slices, analyses were voxelwise (partial-brain acquisition still qualifies). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) with distraction, using an event-related design. It reports within-group, voxelwise random-effects analyses for adults and children (main-effect 1-sample t-tests on contrast images), whole-brain corrected results, and provides coordinate tables and figures. The task contrast includes WM vs control and distraction vs delay (within-group contrasts). Participants include developmental and adult samples. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; thus fulltext_incomplete is false. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Exclusion criteria applied: [].

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (an established executive function domain) that reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level (random-effects) task contrasts (e.g. Space>NonSpace; AlloSpace–EgoSpace) using whole-brain SPM2 analyses with FDR correction and MNI coordinates/figures. Participants are a within-group healthy sample. Whole- brain results are reported in text, tables and figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore it meets I5–I10 and none of E3–E6.

This is an fMRI task-based study of working memory (Sternberg task) in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level activation contrasts. The paper presents within-group contrasts (e.g., average encoding vs implicit baseline; load-dependent linear contrasts) tested with random-effects one-sample t-tests and reports whole-brain corrected results (tables and surface renderings). Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for task-based executive function (working memory) fMRI, whole-brain voxelwise analysis, and within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a GO–NOGO paradigm that assesses action planning and response selection/inhibition — an established executive function domain (inhibition). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects GLM contrasts (e.g., NOGO vs GO) with coordinate tables and contrast images, satisfying voxelwise reporting even though Experiment 2 used reduced slice coverage. Within-group task contrasts are explicitly reported. Participants are neurologically healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). The study used whole-brain fMRI and reports within-group, voxelwise parametric task contrasts, but the task (attending to and predicting target motion) does not clearly fall within the meta-analysis' defined executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met based on available information. Confidence moderate due to incomplete full text; a full article could clarify whether the task was framed as an executive/planning task.

This is an event-related fMRI study that directly assesses planning and initiation of motor sequences—domains classified under executive function (planning, initiation). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (voxel-wise ANOVAs, HRF estimates, Talairach coordinates) with results presented in tables and figures. Within-group task contrasts are reported (IG vs EG, premovement vs movement, complexity effects; main effects vs baseline), and healthy volunteers are the participant group. Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported as coordinates/ROIs. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so the full text appears complete. Therefore, the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based PASAT that targets working memory/attention (executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (whole-brain), corrected p-values, and within-group contrasts (PASAT vs rest; parsed contrasts like repeat prior vs repeat immediate). Results are reported as SPM maps and tabulated coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it is complete for screening. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria. Study is appropriate for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

The study reports task-based fMRI with simultaneous EEG during a mental arithmetic task designed to induce working memory load (an executive function). It includes within-group, voxelwise group-level SPM analyses contrasting mental arithmetic vs reference, and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates and multiple comparison correction (FWE/FDR). Although acquisition used 20 slices, the analysis was voxelwise at the group level, which meets the allowance for partial-brain acquisition. Participant sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusions. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an fMRI task-based investigation and reports group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (test vs control) with whole-brain results (p<0.001 FWE), satisfying I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the experimental task is the Word Memory Test (delayed recognition), an episodic verbal memory/symptom validity task rather than a canonical executive function or cognitive-control task (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet I5 (study assessing executive function or cognitive control) nor I6 (task falls within established executive function domains). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI task-based study of mental arithmetic that explicitly manipulates task complexity to tax working memory. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (complex vs. simple) using SPM2 with FDR correction and presents conjunction and contrast results in tables and figures. The within-group contrasts (complex > simple for each operator) are reported and used in group-level analyses. Tasks target working memory/executive demands (explicitly discussed) and thus fall within the executive function domain. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based PET study of spatial working memory (executive function). It reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (ANCOVA) and both a priori search volumes and an exploratory whole-brain search with corrected thresholds; results are presented as stereotaxic coordinates and subtraction contrasts. Within-group task contrasts are reported (spatial span vs visuomotor control; spatial manipulation vs control; spatial manipulation vs span). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults (n=5). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10, and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a 2-back working memory paradigm (executive function domain). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise analyses (surface- and volume-based t tests, Fourier analysis) and presents whole-brain/whole-head coverage for group analyses (n=12 for whole-head), with task-versus-passive and identity-vs-location within-group contrasts and group maps/figures/tables. Results include voxelwise statistical maps and ROI and group-average analyses, satisfying requirements for within-group task contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise maps. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and include within-group contrasts and original empirical data. Full text is complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and is included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based spatial working memory paradigm (executive function) with both patients and healthy controls. The manuscript reports group-level voxelwise signal-change maps and composite t-maps comparing task vs baseline (within-group contrasts), satisfying the whole-brain/voxelwise requirement. The full text includes introduction, methods (imaging acquisition, preprocessing, group t-maps), results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical).

Full text as provided appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata). The abstract indicates an fMRI Stroop task (I5) and that the Stroop task falls within executive function (inhibition) (I6), so those criteria are met. However, the manuscript content needed to confirm other required items is missing: there is no accessible methods/results to verify whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps (I7), whether at least one within-group task contrast is reported for any group (I8), or whether whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures (I10). Because the full article text (methods, results) is not present, I cannot confirm these inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be confidently applied from the abstract alone. Therefore I must exclude on the basis of incomplete/full-text unavailability and inability to confirm required inclusion criteria (I7, I8, I9, I10). If the full article text/methods are provided, screening could be revisited.

This is an empirical PET study that uses task-based paradigms targeting working memory (an established executive function domain). The study reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses with whole-brain results and Talairach/MNI coordinates, and presents within-group task contrasts (e.g., WM vs SC, WM vs BL, sign vs speech) suitable for voxelwise activation mapping. Participants are a defined group (early bilingual sign–speech interpreters), and results are reported in tables/figures with coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and conclusions, so full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of attentional control (Stroop-like interference), which falls within executive function domains (inhibition/selection). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise group random-effects analyses (interference vs control) and presents whole-brain results in text, figures, and tables. Although slice coverage was limited (15 slices), analyses were voxelwise rather than ROI-restricted, satisfying partial-brain allowance. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI task study with within-group contrasts of selection (select 10/30 > 70/90) in adolescents and adults and targets cognitive-control regions. However, the main analyses were restricted to a priori anatomical ROIs with small-volume correction (3 mm spheres) and voxelwise tests only within those ROIs. The paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map; results are ROI/SVC-based. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI/SVC-only reporting). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (task probes cognitive control/conflict monitoring), I8 (within-group contrasts reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group map).

This fMRI study used task-based contrasts (Magic vs Causal Control; Surprise vs Causal Control) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses, but the experimental task (passive viewing/perception of magic tricks and surprise events) does not fall within the prespecified established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the authors interpret activations in ACC and DLPFC in terms of conflict detection and cognitive-control processes, the paradigm is primarily perceptual/causality-violation rather than an established executive-function task. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI, cognitive-control-related investigation), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (appropriate participant group reported), I10 (whole-brain results presented in text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (task does not map to listed executive function domains). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that used a task-based go–nogo paradigm (inhibition domain of executive function). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FSL FLAME mixed-effects, cluster-thresholded Z images) and within-group contrasts (go vs nogo, compatibility interactions). Participant sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. Results (voxelwise activations) are described in text and tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (image acquisition, preprocessing, first- and second-level analyses), Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function activation mapping and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of attentional control (Stroop), which falls within executive function/inhibition. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise statistical analyses (voxel-wise repeated-measures ANOVA and blocked voxelwise maps converted to Z-scores) and provides whole-brain activation results (tables of Talairach coordinates and figures). Within-group task contrasts are reported (incongruent vs. neutral; incongruent-eligible vs. incongruent-ineligible), and participants are healthy adults. Although acquisition used limited slices (partial-brain coverage), the study performed voxelwise group analyses and reported whole-brain-style results, which meets the review’s allowance for partial-brain acquisitions so long as voxelwise analyses are presented. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of sustained attention (vigilance), which falls within executive function domains. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses and within-group task contrasts (novel and practice blocks vs. baseline) for both cocaine and control groups. Methods, results, and group- and within-group activation maps/analyses are reported, satisfying the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly manipulates working memory load (an established executive function) and reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects GLM analyses. The paper used whole-brain EPI coverage, conducted within-group contrasts (e.g. high vs low memory/attention load; same-side vs opposite-side visuo-tactile effects), and reports results in text, figures, and tables. Participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study examining working memory (n-back), an established executive function domain. The paper reports group-level voxelwise contrasts (2-back vs 0-back) and second-level ANOVA trend analyses across sessions, fulfilling the requirement for within-group task activation maps. Although the acquisition used 15 slices (partial coverage), the analyses were voxelwise at the group level, which satisfies the meta-analysis' allowance for partial-brain voxelwise analyses. Results are described in the text and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI task-based study using n-back working memory paradigms (verbal and spatial), which are established executive function tasks. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain mixed-effects analyses (2-back > 0-back; verbal > spatial), with cluster-corrected statistical maps and tables of peak coordinates. Within-group task contrasts are presented for the healthy control group (behavioral and imaging results), and results are reported in figures/tables in the full text. The sample, methods, and results (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are fully provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

Full text provided appears to be only title/abstract and lacks methods, results, and detailed analyses (fulltext_incomplete=true). Based on the abstract, the paper is an fMRI study of visual working memory (meets I5 and I6). However, I cannot confirm that the paper reports a group-level voxelwise whole-brain task activation map (I7), nor can I verify that it reports a within-group task contrast (I8) or that qualifying whole-brain results are reported clearly (I10). Because the full text is incomplete and key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed, I must exclude the study pending a complete full text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met from the available content.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of reversal learning, which assesses cognitive flexibility/affective switching — an executive function domain. The study reports within-group, group-level random-effects voxelwise contrasts (e.g., CR > BL, PENS+PRE > BL, FRE > BL, FRE > PENS+PRE) analyzed with SPM2 and reports whole-brain results with MNI coordinates in tables/figures. Participants are healthy volunteers and within-group contrasts are provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a task of executive function (Simon task; cognitive interference/inhibition) in older adults. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise group-level contrasts (incongruent > congruent) with voxel- and cluster-level thresholds and tables/clusters of coordinates (whole-brain analysis). Therefore it satisfies I5 (fMRI task-based executive function), I6 (inhibition domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext is complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study of visuo-spatial working memory (an executive function: working memory). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses (fixed- and random-effects), within-group task contrasts (various task vs. grid/no-grid conditions and baseline), and presents group statistical maps/tables/figures. Although coverage was partial (parieto-frontal and occipito-temporo-frontal scans), analyses were voxelwise at the group level, satisfying partial-brain requirements. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (voxelwise group maps; partial coverage acceptable), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant group reported), and I10 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (2-back), an established executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain second-level analyses (one-sample and two-sample SPM99 t-tests) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster corrections and provides coordinate tables. Within-group contrasts are reported (load effects: [2-back>0-back] for verbal and spatial sessions) for both patient and control groups. Participants include clinical (schizophrenia) and control samples. Thus it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and violates no exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the 2-back working memory task (an executive function). The paper reports group-level voxelwise SPM analyses (whole-brain maps are shown and used to define ROIs), and reports within-group task contrasts (main effect of 2-back vs baseline combined across subjects and subject-specific contrasts entered into second-level models). Participants include clinical (de novo, unmedicated Parkinson's) and control groups but a within-group/combined-group task activation map is provided. All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This fMRI study tests working memory/binding tasks (meets I5, I6), reports within-group task contrasts (I8), includes an eligible participant group (I9), and reports results in text/figures/coordinates (I10). However, the authors explicitly state they ‘used the clusters of activation found in that study as a mask, applying those regions of interest…’ and computed ROI-based percentage signal change for planned comparisons rather than reporting group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-activation maps. Thus it does not provide voxelwise whole-brain activation results and qualifies as an ROI-only analysis, meeting exclusion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level task maps). Exclusion criteria applied: E3. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that includes a task-based verbal working memory (VWM) paradigm (an executive function domain). Group-level, voxelwise task activation maps are reported (global whole-brain analysis and regional single-slice ROI analyses with thresholded correlation maps and across-subject paired tests), and within-group contrasts (task vs baseline/control) are used to generate activation maps. The paper contains full methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

The manuscript reports task-based fMRI analyses of a working-memory (feature binding) task and voxelwise whole-brain statistics, but the results presented are focused on between-group comparisons (APOEε4+ vs APOEε4−). The full text does not report any within-group task activation contrasts (e.g., task>baseline) for either participant group, only the between-group t-tests. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I8 and meets exclusion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts with no within-group task activation contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task study), I6 (working memory — an executive function), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (results described in text/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based continuous performance (vigilance) paradigm, which falls within executive function domains. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses (within-group vigilance>fixation contrasts for both schizophrenia and healthy control groups) with cluster-correction and presents maps/tables of activations. Participants include clinical and control groups. All required inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain within-group activation are met, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

This is an fMRI, task-based, within-group voxelwise study reporting whole-brain contrasts and coordinates (meets I7, I8, I9, I10). However, the task is a long-term memory (face–name recognition) paradigm examining episodic vs semantic memory and retrieval processes, not an established executive function domain (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not satisfy I5 (study assessing executive function/cognitive control task) and I6 (task within established executive function domains). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of voluntary self-regulation of slow cortical potentials (SCPs), which the authors interpret as involving cognitive control processes including active inhibition and preparatory attention. It therefore assesses executive/cognitive control (I5) and maps onto established executive domains (inhibition/initiative/attention) as discussed in the text (I6). The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses with both fixed- and random-effects group-level contrasts (I7), and includes within-group task contrasts (negativity vs baseline/passive viewing, positivity vs baseline, and negativity vs positivity) (I8). Participant groups include both healthy subjects and epilepsy patients with within-group contrasts reported (I9). Results are presented as tables/figures with coordinates and detailed descriptions (I10). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function domain). The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses (Z-maps, FDR correction), one-sample t-tests and mixed-effect ANOVA for within-group contrasts (maintenance vs recognition; modality comparisons), and whole-brain results reported in text/maps. Participant group is healthy adults; within-group contrasts are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study explicitly investigating cognitive control/conflict monitoring during recognition (rejecting novel objects in familiar contexts). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (SPM2) with voxelwise NO>NN contrasts and reports peak coordinates and cluster results. The NO versus NN contrast is a within-group task contrast (examined within young and elderly and used to relate activation to performance), and group-level random-effects analyses are reported. Participants include healthy young and elderly adults. Reporting includes tables/coordinates and full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical PET study with task-based manipulations that explicitly examine attentional/control (executive) processes in interaction with learning/memory. It reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses (thresholding, Talairach coordinates) and multiple within-group contrasts (NR-RS, TR-RS, NR-TR, interaction contrasts). The tasks engage executive components such as working memory/visuo-spatial sketchpad, initiation, monitoring, response selection, and top-down attentional control (PFC, ACC, PPC activations discussed), mapping onto the review’s executive domains (notably working memory and initiation/planning/monitoring). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Results are reported as voxelwise maps and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and within-group contrasts are present. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study reporting group-level voxelwise activation maps for task contrasts (block localizers and event-related gap and memory-delay contrasts). The memory-delay paradigm involves holding spatial information over a delay (working memory) and the gap paradigm probes preparatory/ initiation processes; both fall within executive-function domains (working memory, initiation/planning). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses and corrected statistical maps are reported; partial-slice coverage is allowed per criteria and voxelwise analyses were used. Within-group task contrasts (saccade/pointing vs fixation; memory-delay/gap durations) are presented. Participant group is healthy adults and results are reported as voxelwise maps and timecourses. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function) in heavy cannabis users and controls. Methods describe whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM99 (realignment, normalization, smoothing) with voxelwise one-sample and two-sample t-tests and subtraction contrasts. The paper reports within-group contrasts (short-delay task minus perception) for both controls and cannabis users, and between-group contrasts; results are described in tables/figures. Partial-brain coverage (frontal cortex and parts of temporal/parietal lobes, excluding cerebellum) is explicitly stated but voxelwise analyses were performed, which satisfies the allowance for partial-brain acquisition. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, within-group contrasts present, and empirical human imaging data). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references, so fulltext appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract, the study is an event-related fMRI investigation of working memory/elaborative rehearsal (meets I5 and I6). However, the provided content does not allow confirmation that group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps were reported (I7 cannot be verified). It is also not possible to definitively confirm that a within-group task contrast (group-level voxelwise contrast) is reported in the available text (I8 cannot be verified), even though the abstract describes task-related activations. Because key inclusion criteria (I7 and I8) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, I must exclude the study pending access to the complete article.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a 2-back working memory task (an executive function domain). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM analyses and presents group t-maps and voxelwise comparisons; within-group task contrasts (2-back vs baseline) are reported for both patients and controls. Participants include clinical and control groups. Results are reported in figures and text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

Full text incomplete; only abstract/metadata available. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met (based on abstract): I5 (PET, task-based paradigm assessing brain activation), I8 (within-group contrasts reported: rest vs movement and sequence length effects), I9 (participant group reported; within-group contrasts present). Inclusion IDs not met / cannot confirm due to missing full text: I6 (uncertain whether the finger-sequence task was intended as an executive-function task within established domains — authors suggest involvement of spatial working memory but task may be primarily motor), I7 (cannot confirm that at least one group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical map/analysis is reported), I10 (unable to verify the format of whole-brain results e.g., coordinates/voxelwise maps). Because core methods/results are not available, I cannot verify all required inclusion criteria; therefore exclude pending full-text review.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function domain). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise group-level contrasts (NT vs CT) with whole-brain statistical maps (Z-statistics), cluster results, and a table of coordinates for activated regions. The methods describe preprocessing, normalization to MNI space, and group analyses; figures and Table 1 provide whole-brain activation details. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and reports within-group contrasts). Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The article reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (N-back), an executive function. It includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (2-Back > 0-Back) using random-effects SPM99 and reports peak coordinates and statistics for task activations. A within-group task contrast is explicitly reported and used for genotype-based regression analyses. Results are presented across the working memory cortical network with coordinates and effect sizes. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplemental material is noted but not required. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based visuo-spatial working memory paradigm (executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level GLM analyses (SPM2) contrasting delay-phase versus control and uses the simulated BOLD as a covariate to identify brain regions; results are reported as cluster-corrected whole-brain activations with stereotaxic coordinates. Thus it provides within-group task contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results suitable for pooling. Full text includes background, methods (fMRI acquisition and voxelwise analysis), results and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical).

This is a task-based, within-group fMRI study examining working memory and prospective memory (executive function domains). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise, random-effects group analyses and multiple within-group contrasts (e.g., PM-1Back vs NB-1Back; NB-3Back vs NB-1Back). Results are presented in-text with ROIs, figures, and tables. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Exclusion E3 met: the study reports primarily ROI-based analyses (FFA, PPA, dorsolateral PFC) with beta values averaged within ROIs and ANOVAs on those ROI estimates; no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are presented in the full text. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study of executive function — working memory), I6 (task falls within executive function domain: working memory), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported for task phases/load/instruction), I9 (healthy adult participant group with within-group analyses). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no evidence of a group-level voxelwise whole-brain activation map; acquisition was limited to 18 slices and analyses focused on ROIs). Therefore the study must be excluded per E3. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI empirical study using a task (negative priming) that indexes inhibitory control, an established executive-function domain (inhibition). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise second-level random-effects contrasts (NeuI>C, NegI>C, NegI>NeuI) analyzed with SPM2 and provides whole-brain activation results with MNI coordinates (Table 2, figures). The methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Although the sample is small (n=8), that does not violate inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical PET study using task-based paradigms (translation and language switching) that probe cognitive control (inhibition and cognitive flexibility). The study reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM and reports coordinates/tables for within-group contrasts (translation vs reading; switching vs no switching). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy bilingual adults. Results are presented as voxelwise activation maps and tables. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based executive function paradigm (self-ordered object working memory). It reports a within-group, voxelwise subtraction contrast (self-ordered task > control) with group-level statistical maps and peak coordinates (whole-brain voxelwise analyses, noting some superior coverage limits). The task falls squarely within the working memory domain (executive function). Participants are a healthy adult sample and results are reported as coordinates and described in text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusions.

This is an event-related fMRI study that uses a parametric verbal working memory task (an established executive function domain) with both within-group contrasts (each load vs control) and random-effects group analyses. Analyses were performed voxelwise across the whole brain using SPM2, and results are reported with stereotaxic coordinates and tables. The paper thus provides task-evoked, group-level voxelwise statistical maps and within-group task contrasts for participant groups (pre-HD and controls), meeting all inclusion criteria and violating no exclusion criteria. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing complete assessment.

This PET study reports voxelwise, group-level task contrasts that probe conditional movement selection based on arbitrary visual cues — a form of cognitive control/selection (executive function). It includes within-group contrasts (conditional vs. power+precision and movement vs. rest), whole-brain voxelwise analysis with reported peak coordinates, and meets reporting requirements. Participants are healthy adults and the imaging modality (PET) is acceptable. The task maps onto executive processes (stimulus-response selection/cognitive flexibility/selection) relevant to the meta-analysis objective. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/coordinates) is provided, enabling extraction of activation coordinates and contrasts.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a 2-back working memory task (an established executive function domain) with both patient and healthy control groups. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain activation maps (BOLD), stereotaxic normalization, and statistical group analyses, including within-group task contrasts (task vs baseline) for patients and controls. Results and tables/figures describing whole-brain activation are provided, and the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be included.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (voice identity and location), which falls squarely within executive function (working memory). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (Z-maps registered to Talairach and corrected for multiple comparisons), and within-group task contrasts (location vs control; voice vs control; direct comparisons between tasks) at the group level. Partial-brain acquisition is noted (21 axial slices), but the analyses are voxelwise and thus meet the allowance for partial coverage. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based paradigms including a 2-back working memory task (an executive function domain). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects, Z statistic maps, cluster-corrected) and presents whole-brain results in figures and tables. Within-group task contrasts (task vs rest/implicit baseline) are reported, and the participant sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (kinesthetic delayed-recognition), which falls within the executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (Set 3 > baseline and parametric load analyses) using whole-brain SPM random-effects analyses and provides tables/coordinates and statistical maps. Participants are a healthy right-handed sample (within-group contrasts reported). Full article includes methods, results, and discussion (complete full text). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines spatial working memory (a core executive function domain) using task-based contrasts. It reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (memory-guided saccades vs visually guided saccades; visually guided saccades vs fixation) and presents group-averaged activation maps and Talairach coordinates. Functional data were acquired for whole-brain coverage in at least some runs and analyses use standard subtraction/voxelwise approaches. Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported as coordinates and described in the text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only analyses, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study investigating working memory (complex DMS + Sternberg) and its interaction with long-term memory. It reports voxelwise, group-level random-effects SPM2 analyses with within-group task contrasts (e.g., DMS+LTM+ > DMS+LTM−), provides whole-brain results (tables/figures and coordinates) and functional connectivity analyses. Participants are healthy adults. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI of executive function (working memory), voxelwise group analyses (partial slice coverage but voxelwise), within-group contrasts, and reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, empirical human neuroimaging data). Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study manipulating verbal working memory (HOLD vs RELEASE), which directly assesses an executive function domain (working memory). Group-level, voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM (thresholds and voxel coordinates reported, activations tabulated and plotted), satisfying whole-brain/voxelwise reporting; partial slice coverage (6 contiguous slices) is present but allowed by criteria since analyses are voxelwise. At least one within-group task contrast is reported (task effects and HOLD vs RELEASE comparisons; EHR peak latency ANOVA and activation maps are group-level contrasts). Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Results are reported in tables/figures and described in text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and should be included in the meta-analysis.

Full text provided is incomplete (only title/abstract). Inclusion met: I5 (PET task study), I6 (verbal fluency = initiation/executive domain), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported in abstract), I9 (healthy participant group). Inclusion NOT verifiable / not met: I7 (no clear evidence of group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps reported in the provided text), I10 (no coordinates/voxelwise results or clear whole-brain reporting shown). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) explicitly met in the available content. Because core methods/results are missing, cannot confirm required whole-brain voxelwise analyses; exclude pending full text.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory updating (an executive function). It reports group-level, voxelwise (random-effects) whole-brain analyses (parametric regressors and contrasts versus the 0-arrow baseline), thresholded maps and tables of peak coordinates, and ROI follow-up — satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting and coordinate tables. At least one within-group task contrast is reported (e.g., 3/6/9/12 vs 0-arrow, and parametric load regressors). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. It does not rely solely on ROI or connectivity-only analyses and does not present only between-group contrasts. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI task-based empirical study that includes an executive-control task (reverse alphabetizing) designed to engage working-memory manipulation and monitoring, meeting I5 and I6. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level multivariate ST-PLS results with voxelwise maps, figures, and tables of local maxima (peak coordinates and cluster extents), satisfying I7 and I10. The analysis includes within-group task contrasts (e.g., EM retrieval vs Alpha; recency vs recognition) and within-group PLS analyses as described, meeting I8. Participant groups (young and older adults) are reported, satisfying I9. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables/figures, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study should be included for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an event-related fMRI study of a delayed match-to-sample working memory task (executive function domain). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM2 one-sample t-tests and ANOVAs), whole-brain thresholding and tables/figures, and within-group task contrasts (e.g., DMS delay > CON delay; object vs. location; familiar vs. trial-unique). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported as voxelwise maps and coordinate tables. All inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI task-based study that includes a working-memory (episodic/working memory) paradigm, which falls within executive function domains. The paper reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (e.g., EWM > SM) for both healthy controls and AD subjects, with group-level SPM analyses and reported activation coordinates (tables/coordinates), corrected for multiple comparisons. Acquisition used slice-based EPI and voxelwise whole-brain normalization/analysis (partial-brain acquisition would still qualify). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is an empirical fMRI paper with whole-brain voxelwise group analyses and within-group contrasts (approximate vs control, exact vs control, magnitude comparison vs baseline) and reports coordinates—thus it meets I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the tasks are numerical processing (symbolic exact/approximate calculation and non-symbolic magnitude comparison) aimed at number representation and arithmetic development, not tasks that fall within established executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not satisfy I5 (study assessing executive function/cognitive control) nor I6 (tasks within executive function domains), so it must be excluded. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a spatial Stroop conflict paradigm that probes executive control/inhibition. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (e.g., informative position vs. neutral cue contrasts, P–N; W–N; P–W) and voxelwise regression analyses relating preparatory activity to behavioral cueing effects. These are within-group task contrasts analyzed with random-effects group statistics. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and therefore appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Given these points, the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and should be included.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of visual comparisons involving working memory (meets I5, I6) and reports within-subject contrasts (unilateral vs bilateral) consistent with I8; participants are healthy volunteers (I9). However, the provided content does not allow verification that at least one group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map was produced or reported (I7 not verifiable). Because I7 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analysis) cannot be confirmed from the available text, the study cannot be determined to meet all inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met based on the available information.

Full text presents an fMRI task with whole-brain, within-group voxelwise contrasts (wins vs losses; high vs low provocation) and reports coordinates (satisfies I5, I7, I8, I9, I10). However the task is a Taylor Aggression Paradigm designed to elicit reactive aggression and social-emotional processes rather than an established executive function domain (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although authors discuss cognitive control/conflict monitoring, the paradigm does not fall within the predefined executive-function task categories required by I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I6 (task domain).

The study reports both EEG and fMRI experiments and includes a group-level, voxelwise within-group contrast (insight preparation vs. noninsight preparation) with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and cluster thresholds. However, the task is a compound remote-associates (insight/creativity) problem paradigm rather than a canonical executive-function task within the prespecified domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the authors interpret ACC activity as reflecting cognitive control, the task itself does not clearly fall within the listed executive-function domains (I6 not met). Therefore the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

This is a task-based, empirical fMRI study that directly examines selection/initiation and preparatory processes for action and includes working-memory demands for self-selection, fitting executive function domains (initiation, selection, working memory). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (thresholded statistical maps and conjunctions), within-group contrasts (observation vs self-selection and task vs baseline), and provides voxelwise results in tables/figures. Although slice coverage was limited (17 axial slices), analyses were voxelwise and therefore satisfy the partial-coverage allowance. The full text (abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract, the study uses fMRI and includes a working memory task (meets I5 and I6). However, the available content does not permit verification of required whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps (I7), nor confirmation of a within-group task contrast (I8). I9 and I10 cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone. No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E6) are clearly met based on the available information. Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot determine whether the study truly reports voxelwise within-group activation maps required for inclusion; therefore it is excluded pending provision of the complete article.

The study reports task-based fMRI using an event-related Sternberg working memory (WM) task (executive function domain). It provides within-group, voxelwise activation analyses (single-subject and random-effects group-level SPM5 analyses) comparing task vs baseline, and reports whole-brain voxelwise activation and connectivity maps. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of executive-function activations.

This is an event-related fMRI study reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation contrasts (random-effects SPM analyses) comparing task conditions. The paradigm manipulates intentional/top-down control (instructions to ‘remember’ vs ‘look’), which falls under the executive domain of initiation/top-down cognitive control, and yields within-group task contrasts (e.g., high-intention encoding vs low-intention encoding; high-intention recognition vs low-intention re-viewing). Whole-brain results are reported (FDR-corrected maps and coordinates), and participant groups are healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of task switching (cognitive flexibility), reporting group-level voxelwise activation maps (whole-brain acquisition and SPM96 analyses) and within-group contrasts (switching vs baseline; main effects of timing and task-order). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported as voxelwise maps and tables/figures of peaks. Thus all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (fMRI task-based executive function; task within executive domains; whole-brain voxelwise group analyses; within-group task contrasts; participant group qualifies; voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria (only ROI/connectivity/between-group-only/non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports original fMRI data using a working memory (visuospatial) task — an established executive function domain — and presents group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation analyses (SPM random-effects), with within-group contrasts (experimental vs control). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, and whole-brain results are reported. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study of a delayed-match-to-sample working-memory task (executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise within-subject and group-level analyses using SPM99, produces whole-brain parametric maps, bootstrap and permutation tests, and reports Talairach coordinates and brain figures. Thus it provides whole-brain, group-level, within-group task contrasts and whole-brain results in tables/figures. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3–E6 violations). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I7 (voxelwise, group-level fMRI analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (within-group sample reported), I10 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/tables). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 and I6 — the study investigates visuospatial attention and implicit visuomotor responses to graspable objects rather than an established executive function/cognitive control domain (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the task uses cueing and a go/no-go design, the primary contrasts and authors' focus are on attentional orienting and visuomotor processing rather than executive control processes targeted by the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present), so exclusion is due to not meeting I5/I6 rather than missing information.

Full text is incomplete (API error 'rate limit exceeded'); core article content (methods/results) not available to verify voxelwise whole-brain results or within-group contrasts. Based on available metadata: fMRI study (I5) using an oddball visual attention/vigilance task (I6) in a schizophrenia sample (I9) — these inclusion criteria appear satisfied. However I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level statistical maps) and I8 (at least one within-group task contrast reported) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text. No exclusion criteria are clearly met from available information. Because critical inclusion criteria cannot be verified without the full text, I exclude the study pending complete article access.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that used a validated spatial working memory (Visual Delayed Matching to Sample) paradigm (executive function domain: working memory). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level SPM2 analyses (whole-brain voxelwise contrasts) isolating the working-memory component (4s minus 1s delay) and reports coordinates/tables and figures of activation. At least one within-group task contrast (delay 4 > delay 1 / task vs matching) is reported. Participant group (healthy postmenopausal women) is acceptable. Results are presented in tables and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (2-back vs 0-back) in healthy adults. The paper reports within-group task contrasts (each condition vs silent baseline and direct 2-back > 0-back contrast) and a group-level voxelwise analysis using spatial ICA and GLM with Talairach-transformed data and reported coordinates/statistics. Although acquisition covered only two contiguous slices (partial-brain), I7 allows partial-brain voxelwise analyses. All required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using memory-guided saccade and a spatial working-memory task (working memory is an established executive function). Analyses used voxelwise methods (Fourier and regression) to produce statistical activation maps, group-level summaries (mean Talairach coordinates, volumes, group polar plots), and within-group contrasts versus baseline/fixation. Partial-brain coverage (frontal, parietal, dorsal occipital) is acceptable per protocol. Results include whole-brain voxelwise maps, coordinates, and figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, figures, references).

This is an event-related fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise second-level analyses (ANOVA and paired t-tests) with whole-brain preprocessing and reports coordinate-based results for task contrasts. Within-group contrasts are present (e.g., Load1>Control, L2>L1, L3>L2, and target vs non-target paired t-tests). Partial-brain acquisition (24 slices) is used but the analyses are voxelwise rather than ROI-only; small-volume correction was applied additionally. Participants are healthy adults. Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and does not violate exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study of a spatial working memory (executive function) task with healthy adult participants. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain composite activation maps and Talairach coordinates, and presents within-group contrasts (memory vs control; positive vs negative probes). Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. These satisfy inclusion criteria for task domain (working memory), imaging modality (fMRI), whole-brain voxelwise analyses (partial coverage acceptable), within-group contrasts, and acceptable reporting of coordinates/figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function domain). It reports within-group task contrasts (letter recognition vs. letter-case judgment) and uses group-level, voxelwise random-effects analysis (SPM99) with whole-brain normalization and corrected statistics. Results are presented as whole-brain activation maps and coordinate tables/figures. Thus the paper meets all inclusion criteria for task domain, modality, voxelwise whole-brain analysis, within-group contrasts, and reporting of results. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures and references) is present and sufficient for screening.

Full text incomplete: provided content contains only a redirect line and article metadata (title, authors, journal, DOI) without methods, results or analyses. Cannot confirm key inclusion criteria: no evidence that the study used fMRI/PET (I5 not met), cannot verify task domain or task-based paradigm beyond the title (I6 not met), no information about whole-brain voxelwise analyses (I7 not met), and no evidence of a within-group task contrast (I8 not met). Also cannot confirm reporting format (I10 not met). No exclusion criteria from the list are clearly met based on available content. Therefore excluded due to inability to assess required inclusion criteria from incomplete full text.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise surface-based statistical maps and within-group contrasts (cue, delay, response; MGS vs SIR; task vs baseline), with results described in text and figures. Although acquisition emphasized frontal/parietal coverage (custom coils, 24 slices), the paper reports voxelwise surface-based group analyses rather than ROI-only approaches, and the protocol/analyses satisfy the meta-analysis’ allowance for partial-brain acquisitions. Participants are a within-group sample (healthy adults). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based (auditory 2-back) working memory paradigm (executive function). It reports within-group, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM2 with random-effects group-level contrasts and thresholded statistical parametric maps; the paper describes main task responses and interaction contrasts and provides coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable). Results are reported in text, figures, and tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory for haptically explored object orientations (working memory = executive function). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise group-level contrasts (exploration, delay, matching vs ITI; delay-length contrasts) and fixed-effects group analyses with whole-brain voxelwise statistics and cluster tables/figures. Acquisition covered the whole brain (except lower cerebellum) and voxelwise GLM contrasts are reported and thresholded (FDR), satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting. Participants are healthy right-handed adults (within-group contrasts reported). Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, figures, references).

The article reports an event-related fMRI task-based study of working memory/attention (retro-cueing), which falls within executive function (working memory). It provides group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (GLM, mixed-effects group analysis, cluster-based thresholding) and reports coordinates and statistical contrasts in tables/figures. At least one within-group task contrast is reported (e.g., interaction [(Q4 − Q2) − (N4 − N2)] and simple contrasts), qualifying as voxelwise task-evoked maps. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Results are described in full (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is suitable for inclusion.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (executive function: inhibition). It reports a within-group voxelwise contrast (Incorrect Matching minus Correct Matching) at the group level, with whole-brain acquisition (20 axial slices covering the whole brain) and voxelwise t-test maps, thresholding, spatial normalization, and Talairach coordinates for activation clusters. The paper includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). It is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and provides within-group task activation maps. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10, and no exclusion criteria apply. Note: small sample size (n=5) is a limitation but does not violate inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using an oddball target-detection paradigm that explicitly assesses cognitive control/vigilance. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise mixed-effects analyses (FSL FLAME) with thresholding and provide figures and MNI coordinates for within-group contrasts (shape targets > novels; face targets > novels; direct face>shape contrast). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Thus the paper meets all inclusion criteria for task domain (executive control/vigilance), whole-brain voxelwise group analyses, and within-group task contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of working memory (a core executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects SPM analyses (whole-brain), presents within-group task contrasts (WM delay/encoding/retrieval vs baseline and condition contrasts novel vs familiar), and reports coordinates and time courses. Participants are healthy volunteer groups with within-group contrasts reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI task-based study examining dynamic manipulation of auditory imagery that explicitly taxes working memory/central executive processes, meeting the executive-function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (word reversal vs baseline, rhyme judgment vs baseline, and word reversal minus rhyme judgment) with activation coordinates, tables and figures. Participants are a within-group sample of 12 healthy adults and within-group contrasts are reported. Although ROI/small-volume corrections are additionally reported, whole-brain voxelwise results are provided, so exclusion criteria for ROI-only or connectivity-only studies do not apply. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and does not violate E3–E6.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study assessing executive function (working memory manipulation) using a memory-guided saccade paradigm with a colour-coded manipulation phase. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects group analyses (SnPM2) and presents contrasts (colour-coded memory-guided vs fixation; retention period contrasts) with tables/figures. Participants are human adults. All inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that tests neural recruitment for quantifier comprehension and explicitly examines involvement of executive resources (working memory) in higher-order quantifiers. It used whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM99, random-effects t-tests) with full-brain coverage and reports peak coordinates and figures/tables. Within-group task contrasts are reported (proposition+response minus proposition alone; higher-order vs first-order), and behavioral performance is provided. Participants are healthy adults.
