Results include whole-brain activation maps and coordinate tables. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of task switching (executive function: cognitive flexibility). The full text reports methods, voxelwise whole-brain GLM group-level contrasts (one-sample t-tests/random effects), within-group task contrasts (switch vs repeat; main effects and interactions), and tables/figures describing results. Partial-slice coverage is acceptable (they report slice parameters and whole-brain coverage), and results are reported in tables/figures in the text. The article therefore meets all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI executive-function activation mapping and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study (simultaneous EEG–fMRI) using a mental arithmetic task that engages working memory/attention (executive domain). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM99 analyses with group-level one-sample t tests on task-related regressors (state-related boxcar arithmetic vs rest) and PSI-related regressors, and presents coordinates/tables/figures (Table 1, Figs. 5–7). A within-group task contrast (arithmetic vs rest) is explicitly analyzed and reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI task activation in executive function domains, with whole-brain voxelwise, group-level results clearly described in text/tables/figures. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study (3T) reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (complex g-task > simple g-task) using one-sample and two-sample random effects analyses and regression, with coordinates and thresholding reported. The paradigm elicits fronto-parietal activations tied to cognitive control processes (working memory/attention, reasoning/problem solving) and the authors explicitly link findings to working memory and cognitive control networks. It therefore meets criteria for fMRI task-based executive/cognitive-control investigation, contains within-group task contrasts, reports whole-brain voxelwise results, and is applicable across participant groups (adolescent sample). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. No exclusion criteria apply. Overall confidence is high that the study fits the meta-analysis objective of pooling executive-function task activations.

Although this is a PET study with executive-like tasks (Divided Attention, Flexibility) and reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM results and stereotactic coordinates, the imaging was not task-evoked. 18-FDG uptake was measured while subjects relaxed with eyes closed (to capture tonic pharmacological effects) and neuropsychological testing was performed outside the 18-FDG uptake period. The reported voxelwise contrasts are pharmacological condition contrasts (ethanol influx/elimination vs placebo) and correlations between test performance and metabolism, not within-group task-versus-baseline activation maps. Therefore the study does NOT meet key inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI/PET assessing executive function during imaging), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map), and I8 (within-group task contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (tasks fall within executive domains), I9 (acceptable participant group), I10 (coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Excluded on the basis of missing I5, I7, and I8.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a Stroop task (inhibition/cognitive control), meeting the executive-function domain requirement. The paper reports voxelwise group-level GLM analyses and whole-brain statistical maps (group average z-maps) with coordinates/tables and figures. Within-group task contrasts are presented (e.g., incongruent vs. neutral Stroop; Stroop vs. null), and results are reported for a healthy adult sample. All relevant core article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI (simultaneously with ERPs) using an auditory go/nogo paradigm assessing inhibitory control (an executive function). The paper presents voxelwise, group-level GLM analyses (nogo minus control) for within-group contrasts in both alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls, with whole-brain thresholding and cluster reporting. Although imaging coverage appears limited (10 functional slices), the analysis is voxelwise and partial-brain acquisition is allowed by the review criteria. Results are described in the main text (frontal, temporal, parietal activations) meeting reporting requirements. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of visuospatial working memory (a canonical executive function subdomain: working memory). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (including permutation-based cluster inference), presents within-group task contrasts (encoding and recognition vs baseline/fixation), and provides tables of coordinates for activated regions. Participants (pre-menopausal women and matched controls) are acceptable per inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so content appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10.

This study reports task-based fMRI of spatial working memory (an executive function domain), includes whole-brain voxelwise group- and within-group (WM>AV and WM>PV) contrasts, and provides voxelwise results described across the text (with cluster thresholds and coordinates). Participants include clinical (schizophrenia/schizoaffective) and healthy volunteer groups. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of auditory temporal discrimination/timing, not an executive function or cognitive control task as defined by the review (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the paper reports whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (easy–baseline, difficult–baseline, difficult–easy), meeting several inclusion criteria, it does not assess an executive function domain (I5 and I6 are not satisfied). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study examining predicting/working-memory processes (executive function domain). It reports within-group voxelwise group analyses (random-effects SPM results) contrasting Predict vs Detect (and Predict vs Detect 3-back), with whole-brain results presented (figures and coordinate table). Participants are healthy adults. All required information (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables) is present in the full text. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and include within-group contrasts. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly investigates inhibitory control over task-irrelevant distractors (an inhibition/executive control domain), reports within-group contrasts across coherence levels, and presents voxelwise regional activations (MT+, LPFC) and whole-brain observations (pOTS, angular gyrus) consistent with group-level task-evoked maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete for screening. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI task activations related to executive function.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a verbal working-memory (0-back/2-back) paradigm assessing executive function. It reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses (one-sample and two-sample SPM2 results) with tables of MNI coordinates, including a within-group contrast (2-back vs 0-back) and main effects of olfactory stimulation. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (delayed recognition of locations), which falls within executive function domains (working memory). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (delay-period activity vs baseline) and presents group-level voxelwise analyses (spatial normalization-based group analysis with group maps and voxelwise thresholding), satisfying the whole-brain, voxelwise requirement. Participant sample and methods are described. Whole-brain results are reported in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text is provided (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and violates none.

This is an event-related fMRI study reporting group-level, voxelwise task activation maps (SPM99) for rule-based vs similarity-based categorization. The tasks explicitly engage executive processes (working memory, selective attention, response monitoring) and compare conditions within groups (Rule vs Similarity; task effects vs baseline). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (thresholds, Talairach coordinates, activation tables/figures). Participants are a healthy volunteer group (within-group contrasts reported). Results are presented as coordinate tables and figures, satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Full text provided appears to be only title/abstract/metadata; methods/results/discussion not available. The abstract indicates a BOLD fMRI study of working memory in healthy controls with group analysis and behavioral correlations (so I5, I6, I8, I9 appear satisfied). However, the manuscript text is incomplete and does not allow verification that at least one group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map is reported (I7) or that whole-brain results are reported in acceptable formats (I10). Because I7 and I10 cannot be confirmed from the provided content, the study cannot be included. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met based on the abstract alone.

Although this study reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise fMRI contrasts (Ambiguous vs Unambiguous) and within-group analyses, its primary focus is language comprehension and lexical ambiguity rather than an explicit executive function task. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (whole-brain results clearly reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study does not assess executive function/cognitive control as a primary task-based paradigm), I6 (tasks do not fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation; although working memory capacity was measured and inhibition/suppression is discussed, the paradigm itself is a sentence-reading language task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study should be excluded from an executive-function meta-analysis.

This fMRI study investigates spatial working memory (an executive function) using task-based fMRI and reports voxelwise analyses at the single-subject level (n=5). However, it does not report a group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map or group-level within-group contrast: analyses are performed and presented for individual subjects rather than a group-level statistical map. Therefore it fails the requirement for a group-level voxelwise analysis (I7) and thus does not meet all inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI on executive function), I6 (working memory task), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level, voxelwise statistical map), I8 (no group-level within-group task contrast reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

Abstract reports an empirical PET study using the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test (an executive function task) with group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM95) and resulting statistical/power maps identifying task-related regions. These details satisfy inclusion criteria I5 (PET, task-based executive function), I6 (WCST = cognitive flexibility), I7 (group-level voxelwise/statistical maps across the brain), I8 (within-group task contrast/main effect of task implied by mapping activations), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results described). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) appear to apply: the paper is not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical human imaging data rather than methods-only. However, only the abstract/metadata are provided here and the full article text is not available in the supplied content, so fulltext_incomplete=true and confidence is reduced accordingly.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that used an auditory n-back working memory task (an executive function domain). Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (mixed-model repeated-measures ANOVA with FDR correction and cluster threshold), with within-group task contrasts (activation vs control) and coordinates/tables for significant regions. Participant groups (smokers and nonsmokers; genotype subgroups) are reported and within-group contrasts are available. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text (only abstract/metadata provided) indicates an fMRI working-memory task (meets I5, I6) and reports a within-group contrast between activation and control (meets I8). Participants are a within-group healthy sample (meets I9). However, the methods state data were analyzed on the basis of manually defined anatomical regions-of-interest rather than reporting group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps. Therefore the study reports only ROI-based analyses with no voxelwise whole-brain results, violating inclusion criterion I7 and meeting exclusion criterion E3. Additionally, the provided content appears incomplete (only title/abstract and metadata), so fulltext_incomplete is set true.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). The study is a PET face-recognition study using subjects' own faces, not an executive function or cognitive-control task per the review definitions. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise activations implied by reported regional activations), I8 (within-group task contrasts: tasks P and A vs C), I9 (within-group contrasts in healthy volunteers), I10 (whole-brain results described in text). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does not assess executive function/cognitive control using a task-based paradigm), I6 (task does not fall within specified executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) apply. Because key inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not satisfied and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of visual working memory and attention (executive domain). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects GLM, FDR-corrected maps) and provides within-group task contrasts (e.g., WM load 3 vs. 1; difficult vs. easy search) with coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy adults; results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps and tables. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete.

This is an fMRI task-based study of working memory (n-back), an executive function domain, meeting the meta-analysis objective. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses using SPM5 (random-effects two-sample t-tests and group-level contrasts), with peaks and figures (coordinates and tables) described. Crucially, within-group/task contrasts are reported: pooled within-subject contrasts across all participants (Group High_M + Group Low_M [correct 3-n vs. correct 1-n]) and main effect of errors vs. corrects for all participants (Group High_M + Group Low_M [errors vs. corrects]) provide within-group task activation maps suitable for inclusion. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable per I9). Results are reported as voxelwise maps and coordinate tables (I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, empirical human neuroimaging data). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (1-back) — an executive function domain — reporting voxelwise, whole-brain mixed-effects analyses and within-group contrasts (sustained and transient activity; task vs baseline). It provides group-level, voxelwise statistical maps (thresholds, cluster sizes) and reports results in text/tables/figures for younger and older adult groups. The full text includes Intro, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group contrasts). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and is included.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) using an event-related paradigm. Methods report whole-brain, voxelwise analysis (SPM2 random-effects, voxelwise thresholding and cluster extent) and report within-group contrasts (patients: within-subject paired t-tests pre/post; controls: within-group analyses/test-retest). Results include voxel coordinates and descriptions of whole-brain activation patterns. The task falls squarely within executive function (verbal working memory). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; not only between-group contrasts; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an event-related fMRI empirical study that examines action selection/preparation and working memory processes modulated by reward expectation — fitting executive function domains (planning, working memory, vigilance). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM99 (main effects and within-group contrasts: specific vs non-specific preparation; reward vs no-reward; interaction), with coordinates/tables and figures. Participants were healthy volunteers (within-group contrasts are reported). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes an executive function task (2-back working memory) and recognition (episodic) tasks (I5,I6). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise group-level GLM contrasts with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction and reported coordinates/ROIs (I7,I10). Within-group contrasts (task vs fixation and material contrasts) are reported (I8). Participant groups are healthy adults (acceptable per I9). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This paper reports task-based fMRI experiments (N Back working memory and episodic memory paradigms) with group-level, voxelwise analyses (SPM99 random-effects) reporting whole-brain results and peak coordinates. Within-subject contrasts (Two Back vs Zero Back; encoding vs rest) were computed and used in second-level analyses. Results include SPM maps and coordinates for activations in prefrontal and medial temporal regions. Participant groups include healthy controls (and cognitive data include schizophrenia patients), satisfying applicability across groups. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI with whole-brain, within-group voxelwise contrasts are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using the Tower of London planning task (an established executive function domain: planning). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (cluster-level inference corrected across the whole brain) and presents activation results in figures and tables. Within-subject contrasts for planning and movement execution were computed and entered into random-effects group analyses, satisfying the requirement for a within-group task contrast. Participants are healthy adults but the review accepts any participant group. The full text includes introduction, methods (task paradigm, imaging, preprocessing, statistics), results, and discussion, so the provided full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is a task-based PET investigation of reaching that explicitly contrasts immediate pointing versus pointing to a previous (memorized) target, engaging visuospatial working memory and attention processes consistent with executive function domains (working memory/cognitive control). The abstract reports group-level analyses (analysis of covariance and t statistics) identifying regional cerebral blood flow increases across cortical and subcortical regions, indicating voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results and within-group task contrasts (motor tasks vs visual detection; immediate vs previous). Participants are healthy adults, and results are reported in the text. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are met. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Note: only title/abstract/metadata were provided (no full article text like methods/results/discussion), so fulltext_incomplete is set to true and confidence is reduced accordingly.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a Stroop paradigm (a canonical inhibition/cognitive control executive task). It reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain group-level contrasts (e.g., incongruent vs congruent; error vs correct) with coordinates and conjunction analyses. Participants are healthy adults and the paper includes full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/conflict (size-congruity Stroop-like paradigm) that reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (random-effects, p'<.05 corrected) and within-group contrasts (incongruent vs neutral; congruent vs neutral). Results are reported as coordinates, tables and figures and include functional connectivity as supplementary analyses. The task probes executive function/inhibition/conflict monitoring, satisfying the review objective. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of conflict resolution/cognitive control (executive function). It reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (e.g., incongruent vs congruent; high vs low conflict resolution) at the group level, provides whole-brain and ROI analyses with reported coordinates, and includes healthy adult participants. All inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (cued global/local selective attention/conflict task) in healthy adults. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level analyses (SPM'99 random-effects ANOVA; voxelwise F-map used to define dACC ROI), and contrasts isolating conflict (incongruent vs congruent targets) and cue-related activity (cue-only vs cue-plus-target). Whole-brain voxelwise results are described and illustrated. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an empirical PET task-based investigation of the Perceptual Maze Test (PMT), which taps executive processes including planning and rule-following (meets I5 and I6). The abstract describes within-subject contrasts (PMT vs SHAM motor control and rest) and reports task-evoked cerebral activations (meets I8 and I9). Whole-brain activation patterns are described extensively (occipital, parietal, prefrontal, ACC) consistent with group-level voxelwise task maps being reported (I7, I10), but the full article text (methods, results, statistical map details, coordinate tables) is not provided here to fully verify voxelwise/group-level analysis details. Because the available content is limited to title/abstract/metadata, fulltext_incomplete is set to true. I recommend inclusion pending verification of voxelwise, group-level statistical map reporting in the full text.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of the cognitive process 'refreshing', framed as a minimal executive-function/working-memory component. It reports within-group, voxelwise random-effects contrasts (e.g., Refresh > Repeat; Face > Scene) using whole-brain SPM2 analyses and group-level cluster results with coordinates and thresholds. Participants were a within-group sample of healthy adults. The full-text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (task maps onto executive/WM processes), I7 (group-level voxelwise/whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (acceptable participant group), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study that directly investigates cognitive control/executive processes (strategic ordering, selection, working memory, monitoring) during temporal context retrieval and non-memory ordering tasks, using task-based paradigms. The authors report whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level random-effects SPM2 analyses (with coordinates/tables and ROI follow-ups) and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., recency > ordering; stimulus number and response number manipulations). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported as voxelwise activations and coordinate tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an event-related fMRI study of the antisaccade task, which probes inhibitory control (an executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise GLM contrasts (e.g., correct antisaccades vs prosaccades; correct vs error antisaccades) with stereotaxic coordinates and cluster thresholds, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise evidence despite partial slice coverage. Within-group task contrasts are explicitly reported. Participant group (healthy adults) is acceptable. Results and methods (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (simple working memory tasks) meeting the review objective. It reports task-based fMRI (group-level spatiotemporal PLS) with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and tables of local maxima, describes within-group task contrasts and main effects (e.g., modality, task demands, interactions), includes healthy adult participants, and presents activation results in figures/tables. Although slice coverage used 18 axial slices, the methods and group-level voxelwise analyses are reported and partial-brain coverage is acceptable per criteria. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so the article appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical, task-based PET study of executive control processes (semantic retrieval, monitoring, working memory). It uses group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) with multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., SemSp – SylSp; SemVoCo – SemSp) reported with peak coordinates and figures. Tasks target working memory/controlled semantic processing (an executive domain). Results include whole-brain corrected statistical maps and coordinate reporting. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical data present). Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based paradigm (random number generation, RNG) that probes executive control (suppression of habitual counting/response suppression). The paper reports within-subject, within-group contrasts (RNG vs COUNT) and describes significant regional cerebral blood flow activations across multiple brain regions (left/right DLPFC, anterior cingulate, parietal cortices, cerebellum), indicating voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. However, the provided “full text” here appears to be limited to title/abstract/metadata (no full methods/results/discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=true and this reduces certainty; confidence is therefore moderate. If the full article confirms voxelwise group-level statistical maps (as implied by the abstract), it should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses and multiple within-group task contrasts in healthy adults (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10). However, the tasks probe visuospatial and temporal prediction, speed estimation and perceptual judgments rather than established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the discussion refers to working memory involvement, the primary task demands are perceptual/anticipatory/sensorimotor, so criterion I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (executive function) using delayed-response tasks with parametric memory-load manipulation. The paper reports within-group task contrasts and random-effects, map-wise (voxelwise) group analyses and whole-brain acquisition, and presents methods, results, and discussion in full. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria apply (it is not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI task study of visuospatial working memory/attention shifting (executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task activation analyses (random-effects model) with whole-brain (cluster-level corrected) results and coordinates/tables/figures, and presents within-group task contrasts (Rotation+Arrow, Rotation, Arrow, and Rotation+Arrow vs Rotation/Arrow). Although SEM connectivity is also reported, activation maps are clearly provided. Participant sample and methods are described in full. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain fMRI executive-function activations and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study with group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM) reporting within-group contrasts (CA minus FR, FR minus CA) and tables/figures of activation. Although the paradigm is framed as category learning, the tasks explicitly involve maintenance and application of learned rules, working memory and attentional/control processes (rule maintenance, target monitoring, selection), which fall within established executive function domains (working memory/cognitive control). Participants are a healthy adult group and within-group contrasts are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study of verbal working memory (Sternberg task) in healthy adults that reports group-level, random-effects, voxelwise analyses. The paper provides within-group task contrasts (phase-specific encoding/maintenance/retrieval regressors and high vs low load contrasts), uses conjunctions to identify phase-and-load-sensitive voxels, and presents whole-brain/partial-brain voxelwise maps and coordinate tables/figures. These satisfy inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (working memory), I7 (voxelwise group analyses; partial coverage allowed), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (within-group healthy adult sample), and I10 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study reporting whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level task contrasts of tactile object discrimination that explicitly probe working-memory and discrimination processes. The paper reports within-group contrasts (P2 vs P1, P1 vs spheres, delay vs baseline), voxelwise statistical maps/coordinates with cluster- and voxel-level correction, and tables/figures of whole-brain activations. Participant group (healthy adults) is reported. Thus it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for task-based executive function activations.

This is an fMRI task-based empirical study but it does not probe established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The tasks are sensory categorization and self-introspection/emotional judgment, which do not meet I5/I6. The study does provide whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level within-group contrasts (meets I7 and I8), includes healthy participant group (meets I9), and reports whole-brain results in text/figures (meets I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not satisfied; included criteria met: I7, I8, I9, I10; inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6. No exclusion criteria applied.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based paradigm that probes working memory and central executive processes (digits forward/backward). It reports group-level, voxelwise SPM contrasts (digit span tasks vs sensorimotor control; DF vs DB; linear contrast across difficulty), meeting whole-brain analysis requirements. At least one within-group task contrast is reported. Participant group (healthy adults) is acceptable. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of analogical reasoning that explicitly manipulates and measures working memory and relational-integration processes. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) and within-group contrasts (e.g., ANA > CAT, ANA > SEM) with tables/figures of activation, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Participants are healthy adults and within-group task contrasts are provided. The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study reports an event-related fMRI experiment using a delayed-saccade (working memory) task, isolating response selection and maintenance — an executive function (working memory) paradigm. The methods describe voxelwise GLM analyses and statistical parametric maps, selection of task-responsive voxels, and group-level within-group contrasts (reported t-tests across 14 subjects) for task epochs (delays, selection, response). Figures and statistical maps are reported in the text/supplementary figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (working memory domain), I7 (voxelwise task-evoked analyses/statistical maps), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (healthy participant group; within-group contrasts reported), and I10 (results reported in figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a delayed face recognition (working memory) task, which falls within executive function domains (working memory). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise statistical contrasts (match vs nonmatch) and a whole-brain random-effects analysis with Talairach-normalized t maps (voxelwise thresholding), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Results are reported in both ROI and whole-brain maps/coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only analyses, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

The study reports original task-based fMRI data using an oddball target detection/counting task that the authors explicitly link to working memory processes. It reports group-level, voxelwise analyses (spatially normalized, group-averaged voxel segments with thresholded activated clusters) despite partial-slice coverage, and presents within-group contrasts of targets versus baseline/noise (target-synchronized vs randomly synchronized control segments). Participants are neurologically normal volunteers. Results are described in text and figures as voxelwise activation clusters. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria. Partial brain coverage is acceptable per I7.

This study reports a task-based verbal fluency activation paradigm and voxelwise SPM96 analyses (within-group activation for controls and group×condition effects), satisfying inclusion criteria I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. However, it does not meet I5: the activation imaging was performed with 99mTc-HMPAO SPECT (and the PET data reported were not used for the task activation contrasts). I5 requires fMRI or PET task-based activation; SPECT does not fulfill this modality requirement. Full text appears complete with methods, results and discussion confirming the modality and analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Exclusion criteria: none applicable (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study reporting group-level, voxelwise activation maps from within-group contrasts that probe verbal working memory and syntactic re-analysis. The tasks include a short-term verbal memory task (STM-W) and garden-path versus non-garden-path sentence contrasts that manipulate working memory and syntactic processing (executive function domain: working memory). Analyses used random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise SPM with cluster-level correction and report group contrasts (SEN–MEM, GP–NGP) and activation clusters in the left IFG and other regions. Participants are healthy adults (n=18). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplemental psychophysics). Therefore the study meets I5–I10.

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study of deductive reasoning that examines inhibition of belief-bias (an executive/inhibitory control process). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM99 with random effects and voxel-level correction, and presents within-group contrasts (e.g., reasoning vs baseline; correct inhibitory trials vs incorrect inhibitory trials). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI (I5, I6), whole-brain voxelwise reporting (I7), within-group contrasts (I8), broad participant eligibility (I9), and acceptable reporting of voxelwise results (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is an event-related fMRI study of cognitive control (Preparing to Overcome a Prepotent Response), a task within executive function/inhibition domains. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise F-maps and thresholding procedures, and provides regional peak coordinates and tables. Within-group task contrasts (RED vs GREEN; cue- and probe-related analyses) are explicitly reported and interpreted for each group; results include main effects of condition and condition×scan interactions within groups. The full text includes introduction, methods (participants, task, imaging acquisition, preprocessing, statistics), results (behavioral and neuroimaging), and discussion, satisfying completeness. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are met and the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of task activations across executive function tasks.

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based working memory paradigms (verbal and visual) in healthy adults. The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM with whole-brain activation maps (thresholded maps and Brodmann-area localization), and within-group contrasts versus fixation/control as well as comparisons between task conditions. The methods, results, and discussion are fully present in the provided full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations and violates no exclusion criteria.

This paper reports task-based fMRI (and lesion behavioural data) that directly examines initiation/programming of repetitive movements — initiation is listed among eligible executive domains. The study reports within-group, voxelwise task contrasts (single taps and repetitive taps vs rest), with whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses and tabulated Talairach coordinates. Although slice coverage did not extend to the entire brain (partial-brain acquisition), I7 explicitly allows partial coverage provided voxelwise analyses were performed. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of reasoning/problem solving that probes relational complexity and executive processes (working memory/integration/planning). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99 linear-trend and subtraction contrasts), with within-group task contrasts (task vs rest; complexity and distractor contrasts; complexity-level linear trends) and tables/figures of activations. Participants are healthy adults (right-handed college students). Results include coordinates and rendered maps. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete.

Full text provided appears to be limited to title and abstract only (fulltext_incomplete=true). From the abstract we can confirm this is an event-related fMRI task assessing conflict monitoring (I5), the task falls within executive function/cognitive control (I6), and the design reports within-group task contrasts comparing congruent vs conflict conditions (I8). However, the available content does not permit confirmation that at least one group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analysis/map is reported (I7) or that whole-brain results are reported in coordinates/figures/tables (I10). Because I7 (required) cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, the study cannot be confirmed to meet all inclusion criteria and must be excluded pending full-text availability.

This is a task-based PET study that reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps (SPM) and within-group contrasts (e.g., M_SEQ vs M_PRED, M_ROT vs M_PRED, M_PRED vs S). The M_SEQ task explicitly places heavy demands on spatial working memory and attentional/selection processes (an established executive function domain), and authors report DLPFC and anterior cingulate activations consistent with executive processing. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Results are presented in detail in the full text (methods, voxelwise analyses, coordinates, and plots). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is an fMRI task-based investigation of covert auditory spatial attention/orienting in congenitally blind and sighted individuals. While it reports whole-brain, voxelwise within-group task contrasts (e.g., cues>baseline, targets>baseline) and includes appropriate group-level analyses, the experimental task probes spatial attention/orienting rather than an executive function domain specified by the review (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (any participant group allowed), I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task assessing executive function/cognitive control), I6 (task within listed executive function domains). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (abstract reasoning and a match-to-sample working memory task) with healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses (contrasts: R>Rc, M>Mc, R>M, M>R) with FDR-corrected statistical maps and peak coordinates. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Reporting includes anatomically defined ROIs and whole-brain SPM results (tables/figures with coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and is suitable for inclusion.

The study reports original PET activation data using O-15-water during sustained and divided attention tasks in Alzheimer patients and healthy controls. The abstract states voxel-by-voxel t statistics were used to assess activated brain areas and reports activations within each group (healthy elderly and Alzheimer patients), indicating whole-brain, voxelwise, within-group task contrasts relevant to executive/attentional domains (vigilance/divided attention). These elements satisfy inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. The provided content appears to be limited to title/abstract/metadata (no full methods/results/discussion sections), so fulltext_incomplete is set to true; coordinates/tables in the full paper cannot be verified from the supplied text. Inclusion is appropriate based on the available information, pending confirmation from the complete full text.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (executive function domain) reporting group-level voxelwise activation contrasts (e.g., HIGH>LOW, ORG>HIGH) with whole-brain GLM analyses and reported activation clusters/figures. It includes within-group task contrasts, healthy participant group data, and whole-brain results presented in tables and figures. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that investigates memory-related processes during a continuation paradigm and explicitly reports recruitment of a classic prefrontal–parietal–temporal working memory network during the continuation/delay phase. Analyses are whole-brain, random-effects, voxelwise, with reported group-level contrasts (e.g., Continuation vs Pacing, Pattern effects) and coordinate tables/figures. Thus it provides within-group task activation maps relevant to the executive function domain of working memory and meets the meta-analysis requirements.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) in postmenopausal women. It reports randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover fMRI data with voxel-by-voxel (group-level) contrast maps (Figures 2–3) and region-of-interest analyses. Within-group task contrasts for encode/store/retrieve components (task vs baseline/implicit rest and component contrasts) are described and analyzed at the group level. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (nonparametric randomization test overlaid on anatomy). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state only (E4), include within-group contrasts (so E5 not met), and this is empirical human neuroimaging data (not E6). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a delayed-response working memory task with emotional and neutral distracters (task-based paradigm assessing executive function: working memory). The Methods report voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses and contrasts (e.g., emotional vs neutral, emotional vs scrambled) with coordinates and thresholding, satisfying within-group task contrasts. Participants are a defined healthy adult group. Whole-brain results are reported in figures and tables. Thus the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates none of the exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, nor is it non-empirical). Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables referenced) is provided and appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly manipulates and measures executive-control-relevant processes (lexical selection and Go/No-Go response initiation/inhibition). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level random-effects SPM analyses (e.g., Selection vs No-Selection; Go vs No-Go; active tasks vs fixation) with voxelwise and cluster-corrected thresholds, and provides coordinates/tables and figures of whole-brain activations. Although one run used partial coverage focused on SMA, analyses were voxelwise and group-level (partial-brain acquisition is allowed by criteria). Full-text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical PET study using task-based working memory paradigms (3-item static and 2-back dynamic), which are established executive-function tasks. The paper reports within-group task contrasts and group-level voxelwise SPM analyses (whole-brain SPM maps and figures), as well as quantitative ROI results; thus whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps and within-group contrasts are present for participant groups (hypertensives and controls). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI empirical study of attentional control/set-shifting (executive function domain: cognitive flexibility). It reports within-group voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., extradimensional vs intradimensional shifts; reversals vs set change; true vs false feedback) and whole-brain analyses (FDR-corrected whole-brain results and tables of peak coordinates). Participants (n=16 healthy volunteers) underwent group-level random-effects analyses and results are reported as voxelwise maps and coordinates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (imaging acquisition, event modeling), Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI task study that explicitly examines cognitive control/executive processes during cooperative and competitive game play. Methods report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with voxelwise thresholds and contrasts, including within-group contrasts (cooperation vs independent; competition vs independent). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported in figures/tables and described in the text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present, so fulltext is complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive inhibition in healthy adults that reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and within-group task contrasts. The study used SPM99 for voxelwise analysis and reports activations for backward (inhibition) versus motor control and backward versus forward contrasts, with activations described across the whole brain (frontal, parietal, temporal regions). Although slice coverage was limited (16 non-contiguous planes), analyses were voxelwise rather than ROI-restricted, which satisfies partial-brain acquisition allowance. The manuscript contains full introduction, methods, results, and discussion sections. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates none of the exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an empirical fMRI study that investigates proactive response inhibition and executive control induced by cueing methods. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (e.g., mixed-block no-cue vs. pure-block no-cue) with stereotaxic coordinates (Table 1) and interprets activations in inhibition/monitoring regions (superior parietal lobule, precuneus, posterior cingulate, thalamus). The paradigm and contrasts probe inhibition/executive-control processes (an established EF domain) and include within-group task contrasts. The imaging analysis used random-effects, voxelwise group maps suitable for meta-analysis. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and violates no exclusion criteria. Included for meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study reporting group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (satisfying I5, I7, I8, I9, and I10), the task (visual–spatial orienting; exogenous/endogenous facilitation and inhibition of return) probes attentional orienting mechanisms rather than an executive function domain as defined by the review (working memory, inhibition in the cognitive-control sense such as response inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The study’s IOR is an attentional phenomenon and not a canonical executive inhibition task (e.g., Go/No-go, Stroop). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Decision: EXCLUDED because I6 not met; inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10; inclusion criteria not met: I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study that examines visual working memory (VSTM) and perceptual attention tasks (delayed match-to-sample VSTM and related perceptual controls). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM, FDR-corrected maps) and presents coordinates/tables and within-group task contrasts (K-weighted and set-size regressors). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function activations (working memory domain). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that examines decision-making/feedback processing and prefrontal/striatal responses in PTSD. The task engages executive processes (learning, working memory, hypothesis testing, and set-shifting) consistent with established executive-function domains. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level SPM analyses (ANOVAs) with tables/coordinates and figures, and presents within-group contrasts (gains vs losses) for patients and controls as well as phase comparisons. Participants include a clinical PTSD group (allowed). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly assesses working memory (an executive function) using a delayed-recognition kinesthetic task. The paper reports within-group, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (parametric set-size contrasts) for both movement encoding and delay-period maintenance, with group-level random-effects statistics and cluster-corrected maps/tables of coordinates and figures. Participant groups (congenitally blind and sighted controls) are acceptable per inclusion criteria. Results are reported as voxelwise group contrasts and conjunctions and tables of coordinates, meeting the requirement that whole-brain results be clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory/anticipation (executive function) in schizophrenia and healthy controls. It reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps using SPM99 (fixed- and random-effects, conjunction analyses) and within-group contrasts (activation vs rest) for each group. Although slice coverage was partial (14 slices), analyses were voxelwise and group-level coordinates/figures/tables are reported. Results are presented as tables/figures with coordinates. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study that reports voxelwise group-level task activations for working memory tasks involving facial affect. It uses task vs rest contrasts within each group (mnemonic and anticipatory WM conditions) analyzed with SPM99 and reports whole-brain (though partial-volume) voxelwise results in figures and a table of Talairach coordinates. Tasks fall squarely within the executive function domain (working memory). Both patient and control groups have within-group activation maps reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses comparing task conditions (linguistic vs control) within healthy adult groups. Although the tasks are phonological, the paper explicitly manipulates and reports working-memory/monitoring and selection demands (sequence vs single comparisons, pseudoword effects) and interprets frontal activation in terms of working memory/monitoring (executive function). Analyses include within-group task contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise ANOVAs with reported coordinates/tables and figures. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for an executive-function meta-analysis (working memory domain) and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly assesses executive processes (hypothesis generation, set-shifting/cognitive flexibility, and working memory) using the Match Problems task. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (e.g. Match Problems vs baseline; Successful vs Unsuccessful; parametric covariate analysis) with whole-brain voxelwise statistics and coordinates (MNI), and figures/tables of activations. At least one within-group task contrast is reported. Participants are healthy adults (group-level results reported). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study investigating working memory (spatial vs nonspatial) during language comprehension. It reports group-level, voxelwise second-level random-effects analyses (SPM2) including within-group contrasts (e.g., Space > Nonspace), whole-brain thresholds (FWE-corrected and uncorrected) and tables/figures of activations. Tasks map to the executive domain 'working memory'. Participants are healthy volunteers. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study with healthy participants that reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., V+ vs ND, V+ vs V−, V+ vs invalid) using random-effects SPM analyses and reports coordinates/figures. The task is a target-detection/Posner cueing paradigm requiring sustained monitoring and anticipatory allocation of attention (interpretable under the ‘vigilance’/attentional control domain within the inclusion list). Whole-brain voxelwise results are presented and within-group contrasts are explicitly reported. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, empirical data present). Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an event-related fMRI study that investigates conflict related to goal selection and bimanual movement planning — processes of cognitive control/response selection. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level SPM analyses (e.g., incongruent vs congruent contrasts, symbolic vs spatial), with tables and figures describing activation loci (clusterwise correction reported). Healthy adult within-group contrasts are reported. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI addressing cognitive control/conflict), I6 (task probes executive/cognitive-control processes—response selection/conflict, mapping onto inhibition/cognitive control domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (healthy participant group included), and I10 (whole-brain results described in text/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study used a mood induction paradigm (happy/sad) with a gender-discrimination control. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (sadness–cognition, happiness–cognition, sadness–happiness) analyzed with SPM99, satisfying I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the tasks probe emotional/mood induction and simple gender discrimination rather than established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not met. No exclusion criteria apply (E3–E6 not met). Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because it does not assess executive function/cognitive control tasks as required (I5, I6 not satisfied).

This is an event-related fMRI, task-based empirical study that directly examines language switching and its reliance on inhibitory/executive control. It reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (e.g., language switching vs. non-switching; forward vs. backward switching) analyzed with SPM2 using random-effects and whole-brain voxelwise thresholds, and presents coordinates/tables and activation maps. The task probes executive domains (inhibition/cognitive flexibility) and participants (second-language learners) are acceptable per criteria. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied (fMRI task, executive domain, whole-brain voxelwise group analyses, within-group contrasts, any participant group allowed, whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical PET study with task-based contrasts probing working memory (1-back, 2-back, random-number generation), which falls under executive function. Group-level, voxelwise analyses using SPM99 and multivariate PLS are reported, with within-group task contrasts (e.g., 2-back vs reading) and reported activations/coordinates. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Results are whole-brain voxelwise and described in text/contrasts. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a task-based Go/No-go response inhibition paradigm (Error Awareness Task) assessing executive control (inhibition). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (scanning parameters, preprocessing, voxelwise group analyses), Results (group-level t-maps, cluster thresholds, coordinates), and Discussion. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (one-sample t tests, cluster-corrected) and provides coordinates (Table 1), and performs within-group contrasts (Aware vs Unaware errors; events vs baseline). Participants are healthy adults. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a Go/NoGo response-inhibition paradigm (executive function: inhibition). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (one-sample t test) of the within-group contrast Go/NoGo versus Go and provides whole-brain results (tables, coordinates, figures) as well as between-group comparisons. Participant sample (healthy adult males) is acceptable. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of inhibition (GO/NOGO), an executive function domain. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps (voxelwise t-tests with voxelwise thresholds and Talairach-normalized %AUC maps) and describes within-group contrasts (high vs low conflict condition within young participants) as well as group analyses. Results are reported in text/tables and figures. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2 random-effects, coordinates and activation maps) and within-group contrasts (R>NR, A>NA, main effects), using healthy adult participants. The tasks engage executive processes (verbal working memory, response selection/conflict detection/monitoring, initiation/search strategy) as described by the authors, placing them within established executive-function domains. Results are reported as coordinates, tables and figures. Full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (executive function) with within-group task contrasts (experimental vs control; modality contrasts). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (task PLS and seed PLS) with local maxima and hemodynamic response functions described in the text and tables. Tasks fall squarely within the working memory domain. Results are reported at the group level and voxelwise; therefore they meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not between-group-only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory/selective attention (executive function domain) that reports group-level, voxelwise univariate activation contrasts and whole-brain functional connectivity analyses. The paper includes within-group task contrasts (Remember/Ignore vs Passive View) analyzed at the group random-effects level with voxelwise thresholds and reports maps/tables of results. Participant sample and task design are described. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for task-based executive function fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of feedback/decision-making that probes working memory, uncertainty management, conflict monitoring and strategy learning—domains of executive function. The full text reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM2) including one-sample t-tests and repeated-measures ANOVAs, with tables of MNI coordinates and phase and feedback within-group contrasts (exploratory vs. proficiency; gain vs. loss; correct vs. wrong). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults (right-handed females). Thus the paper provides voxelwise, within-group task activation maps and coordinate reporting suitable for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an fMRI task study that investigated memory-guided saccadic sequences and their neural correlates. It meets I5: it is a task-based fMRI study assessing cognitive control/sequence memory. It meets I6: the paradigm engages working memory and sequence planning, which are established executive domains. It meets I7: whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses were performed using SPM99 and reported as statistical maps (Z-values, corrected thresholds). It meets I8: within-group task contrasts are reported (New vs Rest, Familiar vs Rest, New vs Familiar). It meets I9: a within-group healthy adult sample is reported. It meets I10: whole-brain results are described in the text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical work) are triggered. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that reports whole-brain, voxelwise group activation maps and tables of Talairach coordinates for task>baseline contrasts. The 4-choice reaction time (4CRT) task is described as having substantial cognitive load and engages parietal/planning areas (i.e., planning/executive domain). The paper provides within-group task contrasts (activation maps for FT, SRT, and 4CRT at euglycemia and comparisons involving hypoglycemia), voxelwise thresholds and group-level maps, and reports results in figures and coordinate tables. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable per I9). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and can be included in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the Paced Visual Serial Addition Task (PVSAT), which targets working memory/attention (executive function). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level random-effects SPM analyses for within-group contrasts (PVSAT vs rest) for both patients and controls, with activation foci and tables described. Although imaging covered 15 supratentorial slices (partial-brain), analyses were voxelwise rather than ROI-restricted, satisfying partial-coverage allowance. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete for screening purposes. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an fMRI task study with whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts (semantic categorization > passive listening) in healthy adults, so it meets I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the experimental task is a language-based semantic categorization/target-detection paradigm intended to probe bottom-up vs top-down language processing, not an established executive function or cognitive-control task as defined by the review (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The semantic categorization here primarily probes language/semantic processes rather than core executive domains; the authors do not frame the task as testing inhibition, working memory, set-shifting, planning, initiation, or sustained vigilance. Therefore it fails I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an event-related fMRI experiment with group-level voxelwise analyses and within-group contrasts, but the task is a Posner spatial orienting (endogenous/exogenous attention) paradigm rather than an executive function task as defined by the review (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI task-based, whole-brain, within-group study of a visuomotor tracking/motor-learning task. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I8 (within-group task contrasts: tracking vs rest and learning-related contrasts), I9 (healthy participant group within-group results), I10 (whole-brain results clearly reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 — the task does not clearly fall within the meta-analysis’ defined executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the paradigm involves attention/automaticity and authors discuss prefrontal involvement, the primary focus is visuomotor motor skill learning rather than a canonical executive-function task; thus it does not meet I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a resting-state FDG-PET study that compares regional metabolism between OCD patients and controls and correlates metabolic rates with neuropsychological test scores. It does not report any task-evoked, within-group voxelwise activation contrasts (no task-based PET/fMRI paradigm during imaging). Therefore it does not meet the review’s requirement for task-based executive-function activation maps. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/correlations with no within-group task activation contrast). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I6 (the cognitive/neuropsychological tests administered fall within established executive-function domains) and I9 (includes a clinical participant group). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no task-based fMRI/PET activation paradigm), I7 (no voxelwise task-evoked statistical map), I8 (no within-group task contrast), I10 (no task-evoked whole-brain results in acceptable reporting formats). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Consequently, EXCLUDE.

This is a task-based PET study reporting within-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing non-stereotyped (recognition, response reversal, random pairing) vs stereotyped retrieval. Tasks include cognitive flexibility/set-shifting (response reversal, random pairing) which fall within executive function domains. Analyses used SPM voxelwise group contrasts with reported coordinates and regional results. Participants are healthy adults and within-group contrasts are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly investigates motor intention and motor planning — which maps onto the executive function domain of planning. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects group analyses with cluster-level correction and provides coordinates and statistical maps described in the text (MC>NC, MC>SC contrasts). Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., motor vs. neutral, motor vs. spatial), and results are presented for a healthy adult participant group. The full text includes introduction, detailed methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Full text is an fMRI task-activation study with voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses and within-group contrasts (satisfies I7, I8, I9, I10). However, the experimental manipulation and reported contrasts probe episodic memory encoding (subsequent memory effects) and associative/recall processes rather than an executive-function or cognitive-control task falling within the specified domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Thus it does not meet I5 (study assessing executive function/cognitive control) or I6 (task within established executive function domains). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.
